Context: StarRocks-on-Sirius (GPU SQL engine embedded in a StarRocks compute node, "CN"). An SF1000 profiling campaign found four blockers; you are helping choose the best fix for one of them.
Read first: /home/prestouser/.claude/plans/sf1000-top4-fixes-plan.md (the plan: issues, candidate solutions, criteria, acceptance tests) and the relevant findings in /home/prestouser/.claude/plans/starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-planning-cardinality-backpressure.md (sections 3B, 3C, 4). Evidence bundle: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000 (WORKFLOW-PLAN.md indexes it; cn1-cnlog.txt, cn1-quent.txt, card-compare-*.txt, cn1/engine-cn0.log, cn1/dump/ are the raw material).
Source tree (read-only for you): /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf (engine C++ under src/, CN Rust under experimental/starrocks/src, translator under experimental/starrocks/crates/starrocks-plan-translator, StarRocks FE Java under experimental/starrocks/starrocks/fe, engine docs under docs/super-sirius/).
Rules: do not modify the source tree, do not start clusters or GPU jobs, write only under /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/. Distinguish measured facts from inference. Cite file:line for every mechanism you rely on.

Issue: Real FILES() cardinalities in the StarRocks FE. Designs: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/files-cardinality-{surgical,robust,upstream}.md. Judges' verdicts: [

Its cost arithmetic reproduces the code (CostModel.java:129-135, 419-441; HashJoinCostModel.java:58-62, 86-156; EnforceAndCostTask.java:312-327) and its own conclusion holds: the six still shuffle lineitem at 1 CN, and q03 (78 GB lineitem) / q12 (36 GB orders) are predicted to flip BROADCAST->PARTITIONED at 1 CN. Delivers 0.2x-6x estimates, not real cardinalities; lineitem is under-estimated 4.9x, which enters every S_L term. Defects: acceptance golden says FileScanNode prints the estimate 'before predicates', but EXPLAIN prints the post-visitOperator (post-conjunct) count (StatisticsCalculator.java:245-300; q05.costs.txt:342 shows the range already applied on the FileScanNode); getFullSchema() includes columns_from_path (16 B each) in the width; no CI change needed (true). run_mode=shared_data (conf/fe.conf:88) confirms its 4-CN mem term N*S_B (HashJoinCostModel.java:115-127)."

    "notes": "The only design whose arithmetic makes lineitem the streamed probe of a broadcast join at 1 CN (verified mechanism: q03 1-CN today parks orders x customer 146M rows via exch 8 and streams lineitem, card-compare-cn1.txt; report B1). Re-derived its q05/q03/q12 cases with the verified constants: with exec_mem_limit raised (CostModel.java:426-429), enable_local_shuffle_agg=false (:437-440; single-node network cost is 0 otherwise) and the probe-penalty cap (HashJoinCostModel.java:141-156), BROADCAST wins for q05/q03/q12 at 1 CN for any pf; without the cap SHUFFLE still wins (regression path). exec_mem_limit is FE-only here: the CN never reads TQueryOptions.mem_limit (grep experimental/starrocks/src: only the heartbeat MEM_LIMIT_UNSET, lib.rs:507/523). enable_local_shuffle_agg=false has no extra 1-CN side effect because one-stage agg is already blocked by unknown column stats (EnforceAndCostTask.java:411-422). Costs: 3 proto messages, ~600 lines + tests, new FE class, cost-model patch, 5 SET GLOBALs; broadcast_row_limit=2e9 also relaxes PushDownAggregateCollector.java:647; rows_ranges may regress q10 (its own table); q09 prediction is weak (partsupp 800M and orders 1.5e9 unfiltered builds would be broadcast/parked, ~34 GB). Internal inconsistency: summary lists q18 among the five that pass, section 4 case A says q18 needs item 5.   "winner": "upstream (files-cardinality-upstream.md), with the robust design's Part B split off as a separate gate-decided follow-up",
  "reasoning": "Measured facts (re-checked in the worktree at 45dab3be): every FILES() scan is planned at 1 row (StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676, reached from :374-376); the physical FILES() operator falls through to visitOperator (OperatorVisitor.java:454-456) but is never re-derived in the main path (extractBestPlan copies group statistics, QueryOptimizer.java:1112; PlanFragmentBuilder.java:4294 uses optExpression.getStatistics()), so the visitPhysicalTableFunctionTableScan override in robust/upstream is harmless and defensive. All three designs remove the 1-row default; only upstream and robust make the leaf counts exact (parquet footers the CN already parses, file_schema.rs:19-25; parquet 59.2.0 per Cargo.lock:1648). The surgical estimator under-counts lineitem 4.9x and inverts partsupp/orders and part/customer; those biases enter S_L in every HashJoinCostModel comparison, which is what the whole fix is for. Inference (hand computation from CostModel.java:129-135/419-441, HashJoinCostModel.java:86-156, EnforceAndCostTask.java:312-327, all verified): with real counts and stock settings the FE still hash-partitions lineitem at 1 CN for the six (broadcast probe penalty up to 12 vs shuffle cap 3; x1000 above exec_mem_limit 2 GiB; single-node shuffle network cost 0 when enable_local_shuffle_agg is true) and additionally flips q03 (78 GB of lineitem) and q12 (36 GB of orders) from streaming to parking at 1 CN. So surgical and upstream 'fix' C1 (cardinalities) but not the six, and can break two of the 15 passing queries on 1 CN if enabled by default without settings; both say so and gate with a mutable Config plus an EXPLAIN COSTS survey. Robust is the only design that would move lineitem to the streamed probe side, but only through a coupled bundle (exec_mem_limit 64 GiB, enable_local_shuffle_agg=false, broadcast_row_limit 2e9, cbo_cte_reuse=false, plus a flag-gated cap in HashJoinCostModel.getAvgProbeCost); I confirmed its q05/q03/q12 signs with the verified constants and that exec_mem_limit is FE-only in this deployment (the CN never reads TQueryOptions.mem_limit). That bundle is fix 4(d) of the plan, not fix 3: it changes every distribution decision in the cluster, is hand-computed with two coin flips (f, pf), risks q10 at 4 CN in its default mode, and comes with ~600 lines, three proto messages, a new FE class, a missing CI step and an internal inconsistency on q18. Correctness/cancellation: all three are planning-only on the FE plus a larger reply payload on an RPC whose wait is already unbounded (TableFunctionTable.java:713); no CN execution path, cancel path or result path changes; the CN executes whatever fragment shape arrives and fails closed by name on RIGHT_SEMI_JOIN (node_translator.rs:1743-1762) and MULTI_CAST_DATA_STREAM_SINK (compute_node_service.rs:1519), which all three flag with the right mitigations (plan item 5 first; SET GLOBAL cbo_cte_reuse=false, effective via CTEContext.needInline:157-190 and cbo_cte_max_limit=10 > 8 CTEs). Acceptance tests: upstream's are the soundest (fake:// UTs for the fallback at 153 rows, MockUp for the footer path, CN fixture tests summing row groups, EXPLAIN goldens on a clean 1-CN cluster, which matters because the survey had 4 CN ids registered so isSingleBackendAndComputeNode was false); surgical's golden as written ('estimate before predicates') does not match what EXPLAIN COSTS prints for FileScanNodes with conjuncts; robust's is a larger matrix (2 modes x 2 node counts) whose SF1000 pass criterion depends on five settings. Totals tie surgical and upstream at 19; the tie goes to upstream because exact counts are the deliverable of issue 3, PR-A of upstream is the surgical design (nothing is lost), the extra surface is one optional proto2 field and ~40 lines of Rust with zero extra I/O, and it is the only one that already handles the CI patch-apply step and the clean-cluster caveat.",
  "merge_suggestions": "Take upstream as the base (PR-A FE patch with fallback + knob, PR-B optional num_rows + CN + CI generalisation). Merge from surgical: the explicit isListFilesOnly() guard (TableFunctionTable.java:432; do not rely on fileStatuses being empty), the mutable-knob A/B procedure on one FE, SET GLOBAL cbo_cte_reuse=false in the bench bring-up (bench.sh:85 today only defines MYSQL), and its per-query prediction table (section 3.3) as the checklist for diffing plan-summary goldens; fix its golden wording to post-predicate FileScanNode cardinalities. Merge from robust: (1) set tableRowCountMayInaccurate(true) only on the bytes/width fallback path (exact path false), (2) the one-line FE INFO per statement (path, files, rows, source=footer|estimated) and the CN get_file_schema span fields files/rows, (3) the PlanTestBase test with injected statistics asserting join side and distribution (stronger than a contains-assert on 'cardinality: 153'), (4) the build.rs guard extension for the new proto token, (5) its Part B as a separate, flag-gated 'fix 3b' decided at the EXPLAIN COSTS gate: conf/sirius-cbo-defaults.sql with cbo_cte_reuse=false now, and exec_mem_limit / enable_local_shuffle_agg=false / broadcast_row_limit plus the enable_sirius_gpu_join_cost probe-penalty cap only after the 1-CN EXPLAIN survey shows the q03/q12 BROADCAST->PARTITIONED flips it is meant to prevent; this is the plan's fix 4(d) and should be scheduled next to fix 4a, with item 5 (translator RIGHT_SEMI) landing first. Do not merge robust's per-file PFileStatistics or per-column min/max yet: no decision examined changes sign between the 0.25 default and the footer range (q05 orders 0.152 vs 0.25), so ranges add proto/CN/FE surface without a measured payoff; keep the single optional int64 num_rows = 3 and revisit ranges if the gate shows a range-driven decision. Fix upstream's string-equality note (1.0, not 0.5) before it becomes a golden.",

   "surgical and upstream (shared, not a design error but a deployment hazard): with the knob on by default at 1 CN, both designs' own arithmetic (confirmed here) predicts q03 parks ~78 GB of lineitem and q12 ~36 GB of orders in the 100 GiB pool; neither may be enabled for a 1-CN SF1000 arm before the EXPLAIN COSTS survey on a clean single-node FE (the survey cluster had CN ids 10001/11001/12002/12003 registered, so isSingleBackendAndComputeNode was false and shuffle network cost was counted; a clean 1-CN FE zeroes it and makes shuffles cheaper still)."

On the SF1000 tables the estimate is 0.2x-6x (measured du -sb + metadata.json) and every TPC-H decision studied hinges on >=10x ratios, so plan outcomes equal the exact path's for this workload; inverted pairs (partsupp/orders, customer/part) are never joined directly. Does not fix the six 1-CN failures (its own cost arithmetic, HashJoinCostModel.java:134-156 probe penalty 12 vs 3, verified) and predicts 1-CN BROADCAST->PARTITIONED flips for q03/q12 (inference) - shared with the other two designs. Blast radius: LogicalTableFunctionTableScan only; FileTable guarded by instanceof; no wire/CN/CI change; knob togglable via ADMIN SET FRONTEND CONFIG. The missing visitPhysicalTableFunctionTableScan is not a defect: Utils.calculateStatistics callers (QueryOptimizer.java:570,724,908,915) run on logical trees and PlanFragmentBuilder reads memo-group statistics (:1148 scanNode.computeStatistics(optExpression.getStatistics())), verified. One patch file (~50 lines Java + ~80 test), one Config field placed away from the :1212-1223 hunk of files-query-whole-file-ranges.patch so apply order is irrelevant (apply-starrocks-patches.sh is glob-ordered, verified). Acceptance A reuses survey.sh (22 EXPLAIN COSTS + translate-only CN ran 13:00:55->13:01:50, survey.log) with a knob A/B on one FE; golden numbers are deterministic. Weakness: golden depends on the dataset copy's compression (f64 copies of the same tables give different estimates), and the estimator sits in StatisticsCalculator rather than on the table object."

    "angle": "upstream (exact footer num_rows via proto + FE-only bytes/width fallback, Hive rule)",

Exact layer: +3 proto lines (internal_service.proto:647-650 verified; optional int64 is wire-compatible both ways), CN sums FileMetaData::num_rows in parquet_files_schema (file_schema.rs:62-96 already opens every footer, verified; zero extra I/O), handler compute_node_service.rs:688-697, build.rs:70-105 guard extended, CI step .github/workflows/experimental.yml:52-57 must switch to apply-all-patches (verified it applies only the nixl patch today). Same honest limit: does not un-break the six (SHUFFLE 350 vs BROADCAST 718 for q05 even with the exec_mem penalty removed) and predicts the guard (EnforceAndCostTask.java:312-327 verified) rejects q03/q12 broadcasts. Cost: two fork PRs, CN rebuild (minutes), one more patch to maintain across submodule bumps, CI change; its '~40 min fe-build' is unmeasured (pixi.toml:91 says multi-hour; ~/.m2 is warm at 2.0 GB). Tests are concrete and cheap: fake:// UT (1024+2048 B, INT+VARCHAR -> 153, TableFunctionTable.java:589-604 and :259-262 verified), MockUp<BackendServiceClient> for numRows, CN multi-file fixture. Reviewability slightly below surgical only because of the second PR and the CI/proto surface."

    "notes": "Only design that could move the six at 1 CN, but via Part B (cost levers), which the plan files under fix 4(d), not issue 3, and whose Case A arithmetic is self-declared 'coin flip' without the new probe-penalty cap; FE join order with real statistics was never run (report section 5 item 2). Three of its four levers need no code (exec_mem_limit, enable_local_shuffle_agg, broadcast_row_limit, cbo_cte_reuse are existing session variables, SessionVariable.java:1229/1305/1506/1833 verified; CN ignores mem_limit: only lib.rs:523 MEM_LIMIT_UNSET), so they can be trialled on the surgical FE at the EXPLAIN gate in minutes. Unanalysed side effects: enable_local_shuffle_agg=false changes single-node aggregation fragment shapes for every query (CostModel.java:432-436 comment, verified), broadcast_row_limit=2e9 also relaxes PushDownAggregateCollector.java:647 (verified), and the design itself says q10 can regress to 76 GB under its default rows_ranges mode. rows_ranges' hybrid state (UNKNOWN-typed statistic with finite min/max) is coherent with StatisticRangeValues.overlapPercentWith (:73-111 verified) but is the most bug-prone code: Rust decoding of INT32/INT64/DATE/DECIMAL footer min/max into SQL literals, FE parsing, per-column merging. Surface: 3 proto messages, ~250 lines Rust + ~350 Java + ~350 tests, FE patch over 5-7 files (drift on submodule bumps), cost-model edit, new defaults SQL wired into launchers, TUNABLES/DEMO docs; three PRs; 2 FE rebuilds; EXPLAIN gate at 2 modes x 2 node counts with a judgement call on the default mode. Planning-only, so no wrong-results risk; under-estimated broadcasts park builds on N GPUs (bounded by fix 1)."

  "reasoning": "Delivery-side view. The measured failure for issue 3 is data-blind FE planning (StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676 setOutputRowCount(1), verified; card_all_one=True on 22/22 plans and FE est 1 on all 126 exchanges, measured). All three designs remove it deterministically, and all three honestly show with the FE's own cost code (HashJoinCostModel.java:134-156, CostModel.java:419-441, EnforceAndCostTask.java:312-327, all verified) that row counts alone do not un-break the six 1-CN failures and may flip q03/q12 at 1 CN. So the differentiators are surface, dependencies, and how fast the acceptance test runs on this box. The surgical patch is one FE file plus a mutable Config field, no wire/CN/CI change, and its acceptance test is a knob A/B of EXPLAIN COSTS over 22 queries that survey.sh already runs in about a minute (13:00:55->13:01:50 measured). For TPC-H its 0.2x-6x estimate yields the same decisions as exact counts because every decision studied hinges on >=10x ratios; that is the '80% of the value' case and it holds here. The upstream design is the same FE change in a better home (TableFunctionTable.estimateRowCount(), the Hive rule) plus a +3-line proto field and ~40 lines of Rust that make the golden footer-exact and copy-independent; it costs a second fork PR, a CI step change (experimental.yml:52-57 applies only the nixl patch today) and one more patch to maintain, so it scores slightly below on effort/reviewability but is the right shape to grow into. The robust design is really two fixes: Part A (statistics) is over-built for what issue 3 needs (per-column min/max literal rendering in Rust, hybrid UNKNOWN-typed ranges, NDV mode), and Part B (cost levers) is the plan's fix 4(d) with coin-flip arithmetic and unanalysed side effects (enable_local_shuffle_agg=false reshapes single-node aggregation; broadcast_row_limit=2e9 relaxes PushDownAggregate). Three of Part B's four levers are existing session variables, so they belong in the EXPLAIN gate as a no-code arm rather than in this PR. Landing order for the winner: translator RIGHT_SEMI arm (report item 5, tiny) and SET GLOBAL cbo_cte_reuse=false in the harness before default-on; fix 1 and fix 2 before the 1-CN SF1000 arm; the FE rebuild (pixi run -e fe fe-build; pixi.toml:91 calls it multi-hour, ~/.m2 is warm) is the wall-clock item all three share and should start as soon as the patch exists. The fix-files-cardinality worktree already has a packaged FE and the two existing patches applied (verified), so the only new build artefact is the rebuilt FE.",

Take the upstream tests as the unit layer: TableFunctionTableTest fake:// -> 153 with Config off -> 1, StatisticsCalculatorTest over LogicalTableFunctionTableScanOperator (153, all columns unknown, computeSize), PlanTestBase contains-assert 'cardinality: 153', and its TUNABLES.md 'Front end (patched StarRocks)' section documenting files_scan_estimate_row_count plus the now-live broadcast_row_limit / exec_mem_limit / cbo_cte_reuse rows. Schedule upstream PR-B (optional int64 num_rows = 3 on PGetFileSchemaResult, CN sum in parquet_files_schema, build.rs second guard token, experimental.yml switched to scripts/apply-starrocks-patches.sh, MockUp<BackendServiceClient> test) as the immediate follow-up so the EXPLAIN golden becomes footer-exact; define num_rows as exact-or-absent so any future schema sampling (P4 item 7) sends None. From the robust design take: the EXPLAIN gate must include a no-code session-variable arm (exec_mem_limit 64 GiB, enable_local_shuffle_agg=false, broadcast_row_limit 2e9, cbo_cte_reuse=false) at 1 and 4 CNs so fix 4(d) is answered by measurement before anyone writes the probe-penalty cap; the one INFO line per statement (path, files, rows, bytes, source=footer|estimated); the explain_summary.py per-FileScanNode cardinality column for goldens; and SET GLOBAL cbo_cte_reuse=false with read-back in the launcher (run-abc.sh set-and-verify idiom). Defer robust's per-column min/max, NDV mode, FilesStatistics holder and the HashJoinCostModel flag to separate PRs gated on the gate's result. Record in the spec that acceptance A's pass criteria are the eight leaf cardinalities (estimated now, footer-exact after PR-B), q02 join 31 / q11 join 5 broadcasting region/nation, q22 join 11 no longer broadcasting orders, no 'hash join type is unsupported' or MULTI_CAST refusal in the translate-only CN log, and every 1-CN BROADCAST->PARTITIONED flip listed with the bytes it will park.",

# Plan: best solutions for the four SF1000 blockers, and the workflows that deliver them

Written 2026-09-03 15:20 UTC from the report `starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-planning-cardinality-backpressure.md`
(sections 3B, 3C, 4). Evidence bundle: session scratchpad `perf/sf1000/` (indexed by `WORKFLOW-PLAN.md` there).
Working tree for all code: `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/fix-*` worktrees of the sirius-stacks clone,
one branch per fix off `perf/profile-sf1000` (45dab3be = d24f02c4 + aggregate gate + async dispatch + Quent probes).
Never the shared clone `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius`. No pushes, no PRs until asked.

## The four issues

| # | issue | where it lives | measured cost today (SF1000, 1 CN, 100 GiB pool) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The OOM reschedule loop has no feasibility check | `src/pipeline/gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp` (:263 reservation gate, :330-420 reschedule, MAX_RETRIES=100, 50 ms sleep) | q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 take 54-232 s to die (775 s of a 910 s sweep); 17,917 "0 bytes freed, proceeding with partial reservation" lines |
| 2 | No per-query parked-output bookkeeping | `experimental/starrocks/src/engine.rs` (:291-316 process-wide wipe on Err), `compute_node_service.rs` (:449-476 cancel is result-store only), `local_exchange.rs` (removals only in take_ready) | 0-38 GB of a dead query's parked output survives into later queries; dead query's queued senders still run (q22 cold 4110 vs 943 ms) |
| 3 | The FE plans every FILES() scan at 1 row | StarRocks FE `StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode` (:664-676), `TableFunctionTable.java` (file sizes at :611, schema RPC), `PGetFileSchemaResult` (proto :647-650), CN `file_schema.rs` | every distribution decision is data-blind: 1 CN broadcasts 3.79B lineitem rows into q04's semi join, 4 CNs shuffle 3.23B rows for q03; all six failures are one plan shape |
| 4 | Six queries cannot run on 1 CN | fragment cut (FE) + receiver-first full materialisation (`engine.rs` run_fragment_inner, `local_exchange.rs`) + parked repositories outside the downgrade sweep (`src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112`, `src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp:223-300`) | q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 OOM; standalone Sirius runs them in 2.7-6.5 s |

## Candidate solutions to weigh (input to the design workflow, not the decision)

1. **Fail fast.** (a) Abort at the reservation gate when `retry_count > 0 && freed == 0 && retry floor > grant`; (b) abort in the reschedule path when downgrade freed 0 and pool usage == limit and nothing completed since the previous attempt; (c) a bounded wall-clock/attempt budget per original task that scales with observed progress; (d) keep 100 retries for the batch-lock contention case (arrives via `rmm::out_of_memory` from `lock_or_prepare_batch`, not via the gate). Must produce an error that names parked bytes vs pool.
2. **Bookkeeping.** (a) `query_id` on every `ParkedOutput`, drop only the failing query's slots; (b) failed-query set on the engine thread that skips pending `Run`s; (c) `cancel_plan_fragment` drops the cancelled query's parked outputs and dequeues its fragments (needs a by-query removal in `LocalExchange`); (d) `drop_parked` in `run_ready_fragment`'s Err arm for pre-run translation failures; (e) a periodic sweep as a safety net. Order of landing matters: (a)+(d) are pure hygiene, (b)/(c) touch the dispatch contract.
3. **Cardinalities.** (a) FE-only: rows = total bytes / row width from the inferred schema in `computeFileScanNode`, using `TableFunctionTable` file sizes (no wire change; column stats stay UNKNOWN); (b) exact `num_rows` from parquet footers: new field in `PGetFileSchemaResult`, filled by the CN's `file_schema.rs` (proto + FE + CN); (c) later, per-column min/max from row-group stats; (d) no-FE alternative: CN-side translator refusal/hints, SQL join hints. Delivered as a patch in `experimental/starrocks/patches/` applied by `apply-starrocks-patches.sh`, so the FE must be rebuilt (`pixi run fe-build`). Predicted effect must be checked with `EXPLAIN COSTS` at 1 and 4 CNs: the source skeptic warns that `BROADCAST_JOIN_MEM_EXCEED_PENALTY` and zero single-node shuffle cost may still put lineitem across an exchange on 1 CN.
4. **Run the six on 1 CN.** (a) Same-node fragment fusion before translation: replace a receiver's `EXCHANGE_NODE` with its single local sender's node list at the `TPlan` level when every destination is this CN, so the fused plan is the standalone plan (needs `RIGHT_SEMI` in the translator for q21, finding P5); (b) spillable parked repositories: register streaming-sink outputs and receiver inputs with a registry the downgrade executor sweeps as a third tier, HOST-tier `output_row_count` and `export_packed` (five of six then fit in GPU+HOST = 279 GB; q09 marginal); (c) streaming receivers (build side first, probe streamed) is the long-term fix but touches the engine's single-flight lifecycle; (d) FE-side: real cardinalities (issue 3) may already move lineitem to the probe side of a broadcast join, which the engine can stream. The design must say which combination actually makes each of the six pass and what each costs.

## Evaluation criteria (judges score 1-5 each)

1. Does it fix the measured failure at SF1000 on this box (which queries, predicted numbers, how verified)?
2. Correctness risk and blast radius (which paths change for the 15 passing queries; determinism; cancellation).
3. Size and reviewability as an upstream PR (target layer in the carve plan: engine `src/` -> dev PR; CN `experimental/starrocks` -> fork PR; FE -> checked-in patch), tests it needs.
4. Effort and dependencies (what must land first; FE rebuild; proto change).
5. Measurability: an acceptance test that a reviewer can rerun in minutes plus the SF1000 arm.

## Acceptance tests (must exist before implementation is "done")

| fix | unit / component test | SF1000 verification (orchestrator-run, one arm at a time) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Catch2 test in `test/cpp/pipeline/` driving a task through the reschedule path with a memory space that never frees: query fails within a bounded number of attempts with the new error text; contention case still retries | 1 CN, q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21: time-to-fail <= 5 s each (was 54-232 s), error names parked bytes; the 15 passing queries unchanged (warm medians within noise, `compare.py` set unchanged) |
| 2 | Rust tests in `engine.rs`/`local_exchange.rs`/`compute_node_service.rs`: failure drops only that query's slots; queued senders of a failed query are skipped; cancel drops parked outputs; translation failure drops slots in hand | 1 CN sweep in the same order as before: `[gpu_pool] allocated` returns to baseline after each failure (was +4.7..+38 GB), q22 cold no longer inflated, no `fragment run started` for a dead query after its failure |
| 3 | FE unit test (Java) for the new statistics path; CN test if the proto changes; `EXPLAIN COSTS` golden outputs for q03 q04 q05 q22 at 1 and 4 CNs showing real cardinalities and the new join sides | 1 CN and 4 CN sweeps of the 15 passing queries plus the six: plan shapes recorded, timings vs the campaign table, oracle compares |
| 4 | Fusion: translator/CN tests that a single-destination local exchange fuses and the fused plan matches the sender+receiver plan; spill: Catch2 test that a parked repository is swept to HOST and relayed back | 1 CN: q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 pass with oracle MATCH; report their times against standalone (2.7-6.5 s) |

## Workflows

**A. Design exploration (`fix/design-workflow.js`).** Per issue, three independent designers with different angles (surgical minimum, robust design, what upstream would accept), each reads the report finding, the evidence and the code and returns a design (mechanism, files, tests, risks, predicted effect). Two judges per issue score the three against the criteria and pick or merge. One synthesizer per issue writes the spec `scratchpad/fix/designs/<issue>-SPEC.md`. A final integrator checks the four specs for interactions (fail-fast vs bookkeeping ordering; fusion vs spill vs cardinalities) and writes the build order.

**B. Implementation (`fix/implement-workflow.js`).** Per issue in its own worktree: implementer (tests first, then code, build, run the unit tests; commits with Conventional Commits and the Claude trailer), adversarial reviewer, fixer, verifier (fresh build + tests + clippy/fmt/pre-commit). Agents never start clusters or use GPUs other than the one assigned to their worktree (fix 1: GPU 0, fix 2: GPU 1, fix 3: none, fix 4: GPU 2). The orchestrator then runs the SF1000 arms from the table above, one at a time, and an integration branch with all four for the final sweep.

**C. Report.** `starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-top4-fixes-report.md`: per fix, what changed, tests, SF1000 before/after, what is left; plus the PR plan (branch, base, size) for when pushing is asked for.

## Status log
- 15:20 UTC: worktrees `fix-oom-failfast`, `fix-parked-bookkeeping`, `fix-files-cardinality`, `fix-fragment-fusion` being created and built; design workflow launched.

# SF1000 profiling: planning / cardinality / backpressure — evidence bundle and analysis plan

Build: worktree /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf, branch perf/profile-sf1000 = d24f02c4 + 85658f09 (aggregate gate) +
9a5a4da6 (async sender dispatch) + 45dab3be (Quent probes: scan_split_read, stream hops, staging leases, CN fragment labels).
Data: /scratch/sirius/datasets/tpch_sf1000 (decimal TPC-H, one parquet dir per table). Queries: experimental/starrocks/benchmarks/tpch/queries/qNN.sql.

## Evidence (scratchpad = /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000)
- survey/explain/qNN.costs.txt, qNN.verbose.txt   FE EXPLAIN COSTS / VERBOSE for all 22 queries (fragments, join distribution, cardinality: 1 everywhere)
- survey/plan-summary.txt                          explain_summary.py over all 22 (joins with build/probe children and broadcast tables)
- cn1/  cn4/  standalone/                           the three arms; each has runs/runs.csv (query,run,phase,status,ms,rows,start_utc), runs/qNN.rK.out(.err)
- cn1/cluster.log, cn4/cluster.log                  FE + CN logs (fragment run started/finished, declared input stream cardinality, relayed batches, transmitted batches via nixl, OOM reschedule warnings)
- cn1/dump/fragment-*.txt, plan-*.substrait         every fragment the FE sent to the 1-CN and the translator's Substrait plan
- cn1/quent/.cnN/<session>/, cn4/quent/.cnN/<session>/, standalone/quent/<session>/   Quent ndjson (task FSM, data_batch, batch_placement, memory, scan_split_read)
- standalone/runs/qNN.explain.txt                   DuckDB/Sirius EXPLAIN of the same SQL (the stats-aware planner's choice)
- <arm>-cnlog.json (cnlog_extract.py), <arm>-quent.txt / .json (quent_bp.py), card-compare-<arm>.txt (card_compare.py), results.md (results_table.py)
- ../../oracle/tpch_sf1000/qNN.tsv                  DuckDB CPU oracle answers; compare-*.txt

## Tools (same dir)
explain_summary.py, cnlog_extract.py, card_compare.py, quent_bp.py, results_table.py, ../quent_summary.py (per-operator Computing sums)

## Facts established before the analysis
1. FE StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode sets outputRowCount = 1 for FILES() scans ("we don't know the real schema in file, just use the default Row Count now"); every column statistic UNKNOWN. Hence every plan node has cardinality 1 and the CBO picks BROADCAST for most joins (orders 1.5B rows broadcast in q07/q09/q10..., lineitem 3.79B rows as the build side of q04's LEFT SEMI JOIN, partsupp 800M in q02).
2. Engine stream ids == FE exchange node ids; the receiver declares the exact parked row count per stream before build() ("declared input stream cardinality"), so DuckDB plans the receiver fragment with exact input cardinalities, but only after every sender finished (receiver-first rendezvous, local_exchange.rs). Nothing streams across a fragment boundary: the whole intermediate is parked on the GPU.
3. Engine OOM handling: gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp reschedules a task on OOM up to MAX_RETRIES=100 with a 50 ms sleep, then fails the query ("exceeded maximum retry limit"). It does not wait for memory to be released and cannot spill parked batches. q05 and q08 died this way on 1 CN at SF1000 (GPU_SCAN OOM, 101 s and 168 s).
4. Reserving.requested_bytes / peak_estimate vs Computing.peak_allocated_bytes (Quent task FSM) measure the engine's own memory estimation; standalone SF10 q01 requested 20.8 GB for a 5.6 GB peak.

## Analysis dimensions (workflow)
A. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Re-applies Sirius-only patches onto the vendored StarRocks checkout.
# Safe to re-run: skips a patch that already applies (or is already present).
set -euo pipefail

root="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
submodule="$root/starrocks"
patch_dir="$root/patches"

if [[ ! -f "$submodule/gensrc/proto/internal_service.proto" ]]; then
  echo "StarRocks submodule is not checked out at $submodule" >&2
  echo "Run: git submodule update --init --recursive experimental/starrocks/starrocks" >&2
  exit 1
fi

shopt -s nullglob
patches=("$patch_dir"/*.patch)
if ((${#patches[@]} == 0)); then
  echo "No patches under $patch_dir" >&2
  exit 1
fi

cd "$submodule"
for patch in "${patches[@]}"; do
  if git apply --check "$patch" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    git apply "$patch"
    echo "applied $(basename "$patch")"
  elif git apply --reverse --check "$patch" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "already applied $(basename "$patch")"
  else
    echo "failed to apply $(basename "$patch")" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

### 3B. Cardinality

#### C1 (confirmed). Every FE estimate is 1 row; actuals reach 6.0e9

**Measured.** `card_all_one=True` for all 22 plans (survey/plan-summary.txt). Exchanges carrying >= 100M rows on 1 CN (card-compare-cn1.txt, last line): q02/exch3 800M, q02/exch28 800M, q02/exch34 118M, q02/exch36 118M, q03/exch8 146M, q04/exch4 3,793M, q05/exch1 150M, q05/exch4 228M, q07/exch8 1,823M, q07/exch12 1,500M, q07/exch16 150M, q10/exch12 115M, q13/exch2 1,484M, q13/exch4 150M, q14/exch3 200M, q19/exch3 129M, q20/exch9 304M, q20/exch12 800M, q21/exch6 731M, q22/exch10 1,500M. On 4 CNs (card-compare-cn4.txt) the list grows to 26 entries and the summed broadcast rows reach 6,000M (q22/exch10).

**Source.** `StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676` (quoted in P1). Reached for FILES() via `visitLogicalTableFunctionTableScan` (:374-375). Consequences confirmed in source: `checkBroadcastRowCountLimit` inert (P3); CTE inlining always wins (P5); `JoinCommutativityRule` never commutes semi/anti (P5); the translator comment at `node_translator.rs:1918-1929` already records that "the FE reports cardinality: 1 for every FILES() external scan" and that "bounding it belongs to the executor".

**Where row counts already exist.** (a) FE-only, no wire change: `TableFunctionTable.parseFilesForLoadAndQuery` records every file's byte size (`catalog/TableFunctionTable.java:611 brokerFileStatus.setSize(fileStatus.getLen())`, exposed via `loadFileList()` :300); `computeFileScanNode` can estimate rows = total bytes / row width from the inferred schema. (b) Exact: `file_schema.rs:19-27` already opens every footer (`ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder` metadata) for the schema RPC; `FileMetaData.num_rows` is available but `PGetFileSchemaResult` carries only status + schema (`gensrc/proto/internal_service.proto:647-650`), so this is a proto + FE + CN change, not FE-only. (c) Later: per-column min/max from row-group stats for the date range predicates.

**Limits (inference, from the FE estimator code).** Row counts without column statistics leave `ColumnStatistic.unknown()` in place: range predicates on unknown columns cost 0.5 (`BinaryPredicateStatisticCalculator.estimatePredicateRange` -> `OVERLAP_INFINITE_RANGE_FILTER_COEFFICIENT`), IN 0.5, string equality 1.0, and join output = `max(L, R)` (`StatisticsCalculator.computeJoinNode :1219-1240`). That separates lineitem from nation and orders from region, which is what the fragment cut needs most, but it also arms the broadcast guard against mid-sized broadcasts (P3) and gives no NDV for the aggregate outputs that decide q02's join 37. Verify with `EXPLAIN COSTS` on q05/q22/q03 after the change; this was not run.

Confidence: high on the defect; medium-high on fix (a); the predicted plan outcomes are inference.

#### C2 (confirmed). The receiver-first exact cardinality mechanism is correct but arrives too late and is undermined by a flat 0.2 selectivity on the FE's `IS NOT NULL` conjunct

**Measured.** `engine.rs:551-590` sums parked `output_row_count` over local senders and remote batch rows and calls `declare_input_cardinality` before `build()`; `src/include/exec/stream_bind_catalog.hpp:42-47` feeds it to DuckDB's TableFunction cardinality callback. Every declared count equals the actual parked rows (cn1-cnlog.txt `cards[]` vs card-compare-cn1.txt). It only helps inside a fragment: q19's engine plan builds on the filtered part and probes the stream (cn1-ops.txt 6493-6546: `STREAMING_SOURCE(4)->DYNAMIC_FILTER(5)` 3.66 GB -> 0.01 GB, fragment 150 ms) although the FE made lineitem the build.

**BJ-4 (not adversarially verified, medium confidence).** In q10 the receiver builds on the 150M-row, 25.5 GB customer x nation side instead of the 114.7M-row, 2.29 GB stream (cn1-ops.txt 3437-3573: `PARTITION(8) 25.55 GB 0.479 s, CONCAT(9) 0.114 s, HASH_JOIN(14) 0.301 s`; the stream is behind `DYNAMIC_FILTER(11)`, i.e. probe). The translated plan carries `Filter[is_not_null($0)](customer Read)` from the FE's null-rejecting scan conjunct (`expr_translator.rs:630/929 is_not_null_pred`), and DuckDB applies `DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY = 0.2` to it (`duckdb/src/include/duckdb/optimizer/join_order/relation_statistics_helper.hpp:57`), so 150M x 0.2 = 30M < 114.7M declared. Standalone has no such filter and estimates customer x nation at 151.5M. The 0.2 arithmetic is inferred from source, not from a printed estimate. Proposed (translator, `experimental/starrocks/crates/starrocks-plan-translator/src/expr_translator.rs:630/929 is_not_null_pred`; medium confidence): do not emit the FE's join-key `IS NOT NULL` conjunct as a Filter rel (the join drops nulls anyway), or attach it to the ReadRel as a table filter. Measured stake: the `PARTITION(8) + CONCAT(9) + HASH_JOIN(14)` chain is 0.89 s of summed GPU time in q10's 1067 ms receiver fragment (cn1-ops.txt 3437-3573).

#### C3 (confirmed, one correction). The engine's own reservation estimate is exact once a pipeline has history, but the cold-start estimate is 8x, and four cold-start scan tasks reserve 58-80% of the pool

**Measured** (agent-notes/req_hist.py, raw Quent Reserving records). q01: after the first task completes, each scan task requests exactly its measured peak (6.98 GB for a 2.41 GB input, 2.9x); the first 4 tasks of every scan pipeline request 19.52 GB each (histogram `{8.1: 4, 2.9: 103}`). q06: 13.32 GB x 4 then 3.74 GB. Source: `src/op/scan/sirius_gpu_scan_operator.cpp:66 kMaxNumericCarrierExpansion = 8`, `:648-668 no_history_peak_memory_estimate` = bytes x 8 + filter working set; `gpu_pipeline_task.cpp:872-880` takes the no-history branch for every task dispatched before the first completion. Max concurrent reservation held by the 4 slots (agent-notes/bj6_sweep.py): q03 79.6 GiB, q10 75.9, q12 79.7, q14 67.7, q19 58.0 on cn1; the same per CN on cn4 and in standalone. Reservations are charged to the same counter as live allocations (`cucascade/src/memory/reservation_aware_resource_adaptor.cpp:525-531`), and the engine's `[gpu_pool]` running peak reached 99.16 GB (92%) inside q03.r0's lineitem fragment and 106.09 GB (98.8%) in q04.r0 (cn1/engine-cn0.log windows 51 and 65).

Summed request vs summed peak (reservation-ratio.txt): cn1 q11 236.2 GB vs 4.3 GB (54x), q14 15.2x, q03 14.2x, q10 6.3x; cn4 q11 67.7x; standalone q13 549.8 GB vs 0.9 GB (611x, DENSE_COUNT_JOIN path), q14 68x. On 4 CNs every CN pays the 4-task wave per fragment, which is the whole of the higher 1.27/1.64 ratios for q01/q06.

**Join/receiver fragments over-reserve through a different path (measured, mechanism not investigated).** The scan cold-start rule above does not explain the receiver fragments: cn1 q04.r1 F00 (orders scan + RIGHT_SEMI join over the 30.8 GB lineitem stream, 151 tasks) requested 253.1 GB for a 61.3 GB summed peak (4.1x; cn1-quent.txt q04.r1 fragment `...8480`), q07.r1 F08 (217 tasks, four joins) 163.1 GB for 26.3 GB (6.2x; fragment `...753ea`), q13.r1 F04 100.7 GB for 43.8 GB (2.3x). Reserving time in these fragments is 0.002-0.043 s, so the over-estimate did not block them at the 100 GiB pool; it would at a smaller pool or more slots. The operator-level estimates (hash join / partition / concat) were not read for this report; listed in section 5.

**Correction to BJ-6.** The gate did trip at 1 CN: every Reserving > 10 ms in q10/q12/q14 ends exactly when another task releases (agent-notes/refute-bj6/slow_reserving.py: q10 r0/r1/r2 177.1/177.7/174.4 ms for a 20.4 GB request while 3 tasks held 61.1 GB plus 31.6 GB of leaked parked data, finding B4; q12 108.6 + 47.0 ms; q14 128-139 ms), reproducibly in all three runs, 0 at 4 CNs and in standalone. `memory_space::make_reservation` blocks on a notification channel until a release (`cucascade/src/memory/memory_space.cpp:257-266`, `notification_channel.cpp:47-59`). Cost <= 0.18 s per query today.

**q20 partial-aggregate growth (SAJ-6, measured).** exch 9 carries 304,124,949 rows on 1 CN and 639,885,819 on 4 CNs (2.1x) because each CN pre-aggregates a quarter of lineitem-1994 with fewer duplicates per group.

**Proposed.** In `no_history_peak_memory_estimate` use the split's decoded column-buffer estimate (already computed for the history clamp, `docs/super-sirius/scan.md:42`) as the fresh-read basis, keeping 8x as fallback; or cap the no-history wave to a fraction of the space max. Verify with the Reserving histogram (first 4 requests ~7 GB) and 0 OOM reschedules. Confidence high on the mechanism; note that the documented `pipeline.num_threads 8` tuning (`configuration.md:788-800`) would make the first wave 8 x 19.5 = 156 GB of a 107 GB pool, which is the likely mechanism behind the documented 12-thread cliff (inference).

======
## 4. What to do first

Ordered by value per unit of work, with the expected effect and the risk. "Measured" effects are computed from this campaign's numbers; everything else is inference.

| # | change | where | expected effect | risk / caveat | confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fail fast in the OOM reschedule loop when the downgrade freed 0 bytes, usage == limit and the retry floor exceeds the grantable reservation (B3) | `src/pipeline/gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:263` (reservation gate) or `:330-420` (reschedule path) | the six failures die in ~3 s instead of 54-232 s (measured: 775 s of the 910 s sweep); the error names the real cause | keep the 100-retry budget for the cross-GPU contention case (arrives via `rmm::out_of_memory`, not the gate); needs `freed`/`global_usage` plumbed into the reschedule path if implemented there | high |
| 2 | Per-query parked-output bookkeeping: drop only the failed query's slots, skip its pending `Run`s, drop slots on cancel and on pre-run translation failure (B4) | `experimental/starrocks/src/engine.rs:291-316, ~626-643`; `compute_node_service.rs:449-476, 864-905, 1325-1400`; `local_exchange.rs` | removes the 0-38 GB leaks (measured) and 0.4-6.4 s of stolen engine time per failure; restores order-independence of results | Err-time bookkeeping is required (cancel arrives after the next sender started) | high |
| 3 | Real FILES() cardinalities in the FE: (a) bytes / row width from `TableFunctionTable.fileStatuses`, FE-only; (b) exact `num_rows` via a new field in `PGetFileSchemaResult` filled from `file_schema.rs` (C1) | `StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676`; `TableFunctionTable.java:300, 611, 688-712`; `internal_service.proto:647-650`; `file_schema.rs:19-27` | correct build sides, broadcast of the small dimensions (nation/region/supplier), q12/q19 broadcast at 4 CNs, re-armed `broadcast_row_limit`; prerequisite for every other plan-shape fix | alone it does not undo the six 1-CN failures (broadcast memory penalty and 0 single-node shuffle cost, P1) nor flip q03/q10 (guard, P3); needs `EXPLAIN COSTS` verification, and likely a GPU-sized `broadcast_row_limit` / `exec_mem_limit` | medium-high on the change, medium on outcomes |
| 4 | Make the six queries runnable on 1 CN: either (a) same-node fragment fusion before translation, or (b) parked repositories visible to the downgrade sweep + HOST-tier `output_row_count`/`export_packed` (P1, B1, B2) | (a) `compute_node_service.rs process_fragment` / `local_exchange.rs register_receiver` at the `TPlan` level; (b) `src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112`, `src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp:223-232`, `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:822-825, 1062-1066` | (a) reproduces the standalone plan that passes all six at 2.7-6.4 s; (b) five of six would plausibly pass slowly (q09 marginal at ~253 GB vs 279 GB GPU+HOST) | (a) substantial; 1-CN only; q21 also needs #5; (b) medium effort; spill throughput unknown | medium |
| 5 | Translator: `RIGHT_SEMI_JOIN`, and native `LEFT_ANTI`/`RIGHT_ANTI` through the Substrait consumer (P5) | `node_translator.rs:1743-1762, 1824-1860`; `substrait/src/from_substrait.cpp:540-570` | unblocks stats-aware RIGHT SEMI/ANTI plans for q04/q20/q22/q21; removes q22's 6.93 GB -> 0.22 GB filter emulation (measured) | small; validate q22 (7 rows) and q04 (5 rows) against the oracle | high on feasibility |
| 6 | Move `export_packed` off the engine thread and speed up the pack (chunk size / single `cudf::pack`); then concurrent per-destination drains and non-joining dispatch (B5) | `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:~800-887`; `engine.rs:262-330, 813`; `nixl_transport.rs:713-775`; `compute_node_service.rs:160-163, 864-872` | 0.15-0.3 s per shuffle stage at 4 CNs for q03/q10/q12 (10-20% of wall) | (b)/(c) alone gain ~45 ms; packing during execution needs >= 2x staging arena | medium |
| 7 | Cut the fixed FE head: honour `schema_sample_file_count` or concurrent + memoized footer reads; TCP_NODELAY on accepted CN sockets; test `enable_single_node_schedule` on 1 CN (P4) | `file_schema.rs:52-70`; `brpc.rs:110-130`; FE `SessionVariable.java:3337` | 60-110 ms per query from the schema RPCs (measured share), ~40 ms per multi-reply deploy level if the Nagle inference holds; matters most for q11 | the deploy-level collapse for 4 CNs is unsafe as proposed (descriptor-table cache) | high (schema), medium (nodelay) |
| 8 | Staging arena: blocking lease with bounded wait, or push remote frames into pool memory on arrival and release the lease (B6); document `STAGING >= (N-1)/N x largest shuffled stream` | `src/exec/exchange_staging_arena.cpp:213-251`; `compute_node_service.rs:1302`; `nixl_transport.rs:720`; cn-tuning skill | turns a hard failure at ~SF1150 into backpressure | none measured; interacts with #6 | high on the failure path |
| 9 | q15 correctness: compute the CTE once (implement `MULTI_CAST_DATA_STREAM_SINK` in the CN, then `cbo_cte_reuse_rate=0` or stats-driven reuse), or exact decimal sums instead of FP64 lowering (section 1, P5) | `compute_node_service.rs:1060-1072`; `CTEContext.java:157-235`; `expr_translator.rs:808-836`, `partial_state.rs` | q15 returns the row every time and stops scanning lineitem twice (4685 -> ~2.6 s at 1 CN, measured standalone); decimal sums also remove the 9.6e-4 / 1.8e-3 diffs in q01/q03/q07/q19 and likely q10 | do not rely on `SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS` (measured insufficient, 6-7x local aggregate cost) | medium |
| 10 | Remote runtime filters mapped onto the engine's dynamic-filter channel (P2, P5 q20/q07) | translator join lowering (`node_translator.rs ~1719-1860`), CN dispatch (delay the probe scan until the filter or timeout arrives), `docs/super-sirius/dynamic-filters.md:58-94` | q02: ~0.25 s of the 1.0 s excess from filter 6 alone; q20: aggregate input shrinks ~100x (inference); q07 lineitem exchange 59.47 -> ~4.75 GB | large; effort low confidence | low-medium |
| 11 | Cold-start scan reservation: use the decoded column-buffer estimate instead of 8x (C3); fix the q07-type DF dependency (P5 FWJ-3) | `src/op/scan/sirius_gpu_scan_operator.cpp:648-668`; `src/planner/sirius_plan_comparison_join.cpp:646-664` | first 4 requests drop from ~20 GB to ~7 GB, removing the 47-178 ms gate blocks at 1 CN and enabling more pipeline slots; ~0.25-0.3 s in q07's join fragment | verify no OOM reschedules appear | high (estimate), medium (DF) |
| 12 | Tooling: fix `quent_bp.py` lease attribution and `scan_reads` keys; split `scan_split_read` into read and decode (AGG-6, B7) | `scratchpad/perf/sf1000/quent_bp.py:60-70, 98-104`; `src/op/scan/sirius_gpu_scan_operator.cpp:600-632`, `src/include/telemetry/scan_telemetry.hpp:34` | correct per-query lease totals; attributable 4-CN scan slowdown | none | high |

Available today without code changes, for experiments only: SQL join hints (`JOIN [BROADCAST|SHUFFLE]`, need explicit JOIN syntax and pin order), `broadcast_row_limit`, `enable_single_node_schedule` (1 CN), and for q16 the `SET new_planner_agg_stage = 1` that the CN's own error text suggests (not exercised in this campaign; whether the single-stage `multi_distinct_count` then translates is unknown). Nothing available today un-breaks q05/q08/q09/q17/q18/q21 on 1 CN.

---

## 5. Open questions and what was not measured

1. **4-CN behaviour of q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21.** Never run (cn4/runs/runs.csv). The per-CN parked lineitem share would be ~31-61 GB, so passing is expected, but q09's per-CN share (61 GB) plus its other shuffled streams is untested, and the 4-CN plans differ in shape (q21).
2. **FE plans with real statistics.** No `EXPLAIN COSTS` was run with FILES() row counts or column statistics; the predicted outcomes in P1/P3 (broadcast penalty, guard, width rule) are hand computations of the cost code. The hint experiments (P3) were not run.
3. **Cause of the 1.3-1.6x per-task scan slowdown at 4 CNs and the q01 0.5-0.87 s split stalls** (B7). The probe cannot separate file read from decode and the digest dropped its bytes. Also open: the q02 4-CN partsupp fragment that reads at 0.21 s/GB while its sibling reads at 0.05 s/GB in the same run (MFS-5).
4. **Whether the deploy-level gaps are Nagle/delayed ACK** (P4): inferred from the pattern (gaps only after multi-reply levels) and the absence of `set_nodelay` on accepted sockets; a one-line test exists.
5. **q10's oracle mismatch**: resolved (section 1): same 20 customers, revenue sums low by up to 3.7e-3, five rows reordered; no remaining open question beyond the decimal lowering itself (section 4, item 9).
6. **q11 returns 0 rows on both engines** because the bench kit does not scale the 0.0001 fraction; the compare cannot confirm correctness of q11 at SF1000.
7. **cn1 timings of q10-q16 and q22.r1/r2 were taken with 31.6 / 36.6 GB of leaked parked output in the pool** (B4). Re-run on a clean CN before quoting them; the reservation-gate blocks in C3 depend on that leak.
8. **Sample size.** Warm medians are n=2; cn4 q02 has a 21% spread (1264 vs 1044 ms) that tracks one partsupp scan fragment; the six failures and their standalone counterparts ran once each.
9. **Can the engine run two fragments concurrently on one `SiriusContext`?** The single-flight `query_lifecycle_mutex_` and shared `task_creator_` say no today; the cost of lifting that (needed for streaming receivers, B1 route 2) was not scoped.
10. **Host spill throughput.** B2's "five of six would pass" assumes a working spill at 279 GB GPU+HOST; no spill bandwidth was measured, and q09 is marginal.
11. **`enable_single_node_schedule` with FILES()** qualifies by code reading (`JobSpec.supportSingleNodeParallelSchedule`, `ScanNode.isConnectorScanNode`) but was not exercised.
12. **The receive-side unpack at 2.1 TB/s vs the pack at 63 GB/s** points at the 8 MiB `chunked_pack` (B5) but no alternative pack was timed.
13. **Standalone q11 scans partsupp once** (Quent shows one 16.4 GB GPU_SCAN for two CTE_SCANs) while the plan shows a CTE with two consumers; how the second consumer is served was not pursued.
14. **Session cold start.** cn1 q01 cold 9359 ms vs 5073 warm: the first fragment's summed `GPU_SCAN` was 25.9 s vs 12.2 s (cn1-quent.txt q01.r0 / r1), i.e. the very first GPU scan of the CN process runs ~2x slower per split; standalone's first query shows a smaller version (Comp 23.0 vs 19.0 s). Not separated into GPFS/O_DIRECT first-touch, CUDA module load, or pool warm-up.
15. **Standalone warm-run spread.** standalone q03 2479/3622 ms and q04 2113/1678 ms (runs.csv); the slow q03 run is a slow scan (standalone-quent.txt lines 43-54: `GPU_SCAN(10)` 11.24 s vs 7.20 s summed). With n=2 the q03/q04 1-CN parity ratios (1.02/0.98) are not distinguishable from 1.1-1.25. Re-run with n>=5 before quoting parity for these two.
16. **Join-fragment over-reservation.** q04 F00 253 GB requested for 61 GB peak, q07 F08 163 GB for 26 GB (C3). The hash-join / partition / concat reservation estimates were not read; whether they use a no-history multiplier like the scan's 8x is unknown.
17. **q16 workaround.** `SET new_planner_agg_stage = 1` is only the CN's error-text suggestion; not run. q16 also has the same partsupp-broadcast (exch 2) and `NULL AWARE LEFT ANTI JOIN (BROADCAST)` on supplier (exch 7) shape as the other WITH queries (survey/plan-summary.txt line 32), so it will inherit P2/P5 once it translates.
18. **Shuffle skew at 4 CNs** (P3): q07 exch 20 2.7x, q02 exch 31 one empty CN, q11 exch 4 2.7x, all on low-NDV nation/region keys. No wall-clock loss was attributable at these volumes; not measured for a shuffle where the skewed stream is the large one.
