content.content:
## 3. Findings by dimension

Notation: **P** planning, **C** cardinality, **B** backpressure. Confirmed findings first in each dimension (both a data skeptic and a source skeptic failed to refute them; their corrections are folded in), then disputed findings with the objection stated, then lower-ranked findings that were not adversarially verified (marked as such).

### 3A. Planning

#### P1 (confirmed). The six 1-CN failures are one FE plan shape: an unfiltered lineitem leaf feeding a hash-partitioned exchange, whose whole output must be parked on the GPU

**Measured.** In all six plans the failing fragment is a bare lineitem `FileScanNode` under a `HASH_PARTITIONED` `TDataStreamSink` with one destination (survey/plan-summary.txt lines 10, 16, 18, 34, 36, 42; dumps cn1/dump/fragment-0141 (q05, node 8), 0208 (q08), 0220 (q09), 0427 (q17, node 0), 0437 (q18, node 9), 0504 (q21, node 12), each `output_partition TPartitionType(2)` = HASH_PARTITIONED per `Partitions.thrift:41-49`). The FE join labels differ (q05/q08/q09/q17 PARTITIONED, q18 `11:INNER JOIN (BUCKET_SHUFFLE(S))`, q21 `14:LEFT SEMI JOIN (BUCKET_SHUFFLE(S))`), the sink type does not. Lineitem is the build-side exchange in five plans and the probe-side exchange in q17. Every one of the six failing fragments was started as `role=sender inputs=0 outputs=1` (cn1/cluster.log lines 4200, 7854, 9840, 16770, 18095, 20282).

Because nothing streams across a fragment boundary (finding B1), the sender must park its entire projection. Size of that projection (standalone `GPU_SCAN in=` of the same scan, agent-notes/standalone-failed-quent.txt) versus what fit before the pool filled (cn1-quent.txt `STREAMING_SINK in=`, engine-cn0.log `[gpu_pool] QueryBegin/QueryEnd allocated=`):

| query | lineitem projection (GB) | pool before the sender started (GB) | parked by the sender at death (GB) | pool at death (GB) | stuck tasks x 100 retries |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| q05 | 171.00 | 0.00 | 104.30 | 104.30 | 25 |
| q08 | 195.75 | 4.70 (q05 leftovers) | 99.54 | 104.24 | 36 |
| q09 | 244.50 | 8.83 (q08 leftovers) | 96.42 | 105.24 | 56 |
| q17 | 122.25 | 38.16 (q09 + q16 leftovers) | 66.26 | 104.42 | 21 |
| q18 | 97.50 | 68.69 (own senders: customer 3.94 + agg 24.0 + orders 36.75, plus 4.0 q17 leftover) | 35.87 | 104.56 | 23 |
| q21 | 73.50 (the 28-task l2 leaf) | 77.76 (own filtered l1/l3 sender) | 25.37 | 103.14 | 18 |

Pool cap = 107,374,182,400 bytes (100 GiB); every one of the 17,917 OOM lines in cn1/engine-cn0.log reads `global usage 107374182400 bytes`. `begin + parked = end` holds within 0.01 GB in every row.

Correction to the original claim: "the sender cannot fit its own output" is true for q05/q08/q09/q17 (projection > 107 GB alone) but not for q18 (97.5 GB) or q21 (73.5 GB), which died because the query's other exchange inputs were parked at the same time. The accurate statement is: the sum of concurrently parked exchange inputs of one query (plus leftovers of earlier failed queries, finding B4) exceeds the pool, and nothing can be spilled (finding B2). Per-row widths in the engine are 12-41 B (decimals arrive as 8-byte values), so the analyst's "168-456 GB" range with decimal128 widths overstates three of the six.

**Measured, standalone contrast.** The same SQL on the same GPU and pool passes because DuckDB's stats-aware plan streams lineitem as the probe of a hash join built on the small filtered dimension chain: standalone-failed/runs/q05.explain.txt:50-61 has `READ_PARQUET lineitem ~6,110,827,680 rows` as the probe child with a ~61.6M-row build; q18.explain.txt:37-56 likewise; q17/q21 use DELIM joins. standalone-failed-quent q17 `HASH_JOIN(18) n=46 in=120.54 GB` shows lineitem probing in 46 batches, never materialised. Standalone still materialises lineitem-derived aggregate state (q18 PARTITION(5) 36.19 GB), just not the raw projection.

**Root cause.** `StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode` (FE `sql/optimizer/statistics/StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676`): `// cause we don't know the real schema in file, just use the default Row Count now` `builder.setOutputRowCount(1)`, every column `ColumnStatistic.unknown()`. card-compare-cn1.txt shows FE estimate 1 for every exchange of the six queries against actuals of 150,000,000 / 227,571,151 (q05 s1/s4) and 730,806,711 (q21 s6). With every side at 1 row the CBO's fragment cut is arithmetic on column widths and node count (finding P3).

**Not measured.** Whether the six pass on 4 CNs. cn4/runs/runs.csv has no rows for them. A hash-partitioned exchange splits parked bytes across CNs (cn4 q03.r1: the 3.23B-row lineitem shuffle parked 19.60/19.67/19.71/19.86 GB per CN), so the per-CN lineitem share would be ~31-61 GB and the expected outcome is pass (inference). The 4-CN plans are also not identical: q21's `10:RIGHT ANTI JOIN` becomes `BUCKET_SHUFFLE(S)` with a local build (plan-summary-4cn.txt line 42).

**Proposed changes.**

1. FE: real FILES() cardinalities (finding C1, section 4 item 3). Caveat from the source skeptic (inference, medium confidence): with real statistics the small side of lineitem's join is orders-derived (q18 ~308M rows, q05 227M rows, tens of GB), `CostModel.java:428` multiplies a broadcast whose build exceeds `exec_mem_limit` (2 GiB, `SessionVariable.java:1305`) by `BROADCAST_JOIN_MEM_EXCEED_PENALTY` = 1000, and the shuffle network cost is 0 on a single node (`CostModel.java:437-440`). Real row counts alone may therefore still put lineitem across an exchange on 1 CN; this needs an `EXPLAIN COSTS` with statistics, which was not run.
2. CN, 1-CN only: fuse a leaf scan fragment into its single-destination receiver before translation, at the `TPlan` level (replace the receiver's `EXCHANGE_NODE` with the sender's node list; `ExchangeNode.java:183/360` guarantee the row layout matches). On 1 CN every exchange is local, so the fused plan is the standalone plan that passes all six. Substantial work; medium confidence. Caveat: for q21 the fused lineitem would sit on the build side of a `LEFT SEMI` that the translator cannot flip (no `RIGHT_SEMI`, finding P5), so q21 needs P5 as well.
3. Engine: fail fast (finding B3) so a wrong plan costs ~3 s instead of 54-232 s.

Confidence: high on the diagnosis; medium on which fix path is accepted.

#### P2 (confirmed). q02: the FE decorrelates the min-subquery into a full 800M-row partsupp chain and shuffles a 1-row region; its runtime filters are dropped by the CN

**Measured, 1 CN.** card-compare-cn1.txt lines 4-15: exch 3 BROADCAST 800,000,000 rows (partsupp as the build of join 4); exch 28 SHUFFLE 800,000,000 by `n_regionkey` into join 31 PARTITIONED against exch 30 = 1 row (region EUROPE); exch 34/36 = 118,065,576-row min table. survey/explain/q02.costs.txt:305-327 (join 31), 519-535 (join 4), 73-97 (join 37 `build runtime filters filter_id=7 build_expr=ps_partkey remote=true`).

The engine rescues the build side inside F00: cn1-quent.txt:118-122 fragment 56c `DYNAMIC_FILTER(4) n=5 in=13.10GB` -> 0.05 GB, `HASH_JOIN(7)` input 0.07 GB (DuckDB inside the fragment built on the filtered part and join-filtered the parked partsupp stream). The 13.1 GB partsupp stream was still scanned and parked in full (fragment 56d GPU_SCAN 0.788 s). The cost that is not rescued is the subquery chain: fragment 566 (F11, partsupp x supplier x nation) `GPU_SCAN(6) 0.779 + HASH_JOIN(10) 0.289 + HASH_JOIN(14) 0.399 s`, wall 438 ms of a 1.063 s span (41%), plus F19 `HASH_JOIN(7) 0.243 s` over 13.0 GB and the min aggregation. Standalone (standalone-quent.txt:25-30) spends 1.826 s Computing of which 1.769 s is GPU_SCAN (it also scans partsupp twice) and 0.057 s everything else; its `LEFT_DELIM_JOIN` (standalone/runs/q02.explain.txt:52, 142-157) joins the subquery's partsupp with `DELIM_SCAN` (the outer's distinct p_partkeys) before the min aggregation. cn1 Computing 2.9 s vs standalone 1.8 s (reservation-ratio.txt lines 4, 34): the ~1.0 s excess is joins and aggregates over 800M rows.

Runtime filters are dropped, measured: the FE attached filter 6 (`r_regionkey` -> F14 nation scan) and shipped `TRuntimeFilterDescription` entries with `has_remote_targets: true` (cn1/dump/fragment-0025.txt:1074-1275), yet exch 25 delivered all 25 nations (card-compare-cn1.txt, q02 exch 25 row), so exch 28 carried 800M rows instead of ~160M. `grep -rn runtime_filter` over `crates/starrocks-plan-translator/src` and `experimental/starrocks/src` finds only a test fixture (wire_type_parity.rs:607).

**Measured, 4 CN.** The plan changes (13 -> 16 fragments): exch 4, 21, 26, 31 = 800,000,000 rows each (card-compare-cn4.txt lines 4-18; two are raw partsupp scans, two are re-shuffles of the joined 800M-row intermediate on `s_nationkey` and `n_regionkey`), exch 39 BROADCAST = 118,065,576 rows delivered to 4 CNs (card_compare sums receivers, hence "472M"). 135 nixl transmits, 43.6-45.7 GB per run (cn4-transmits.txt). The `n_regionkey` shuffle (5 distinct values) is skewed: cn4-cnlog.json q02.r0 stream 31 per receiver = 479,981,680 / 160,046,880 / 159,971,440 / 0 rows. Total Computing went from 2.9 s to 4.6 s over 4 CNs = 1.15 s per CN, but the span did not move (1.063 -> 1.077 s), Queued = 0: q02 on 4 CNs is wait-dominated.

Two further q02 facts: ~200 ms of the 1-CN vs standalone gap is outside the engine span (finding P4), and on 4 CNs one of the two partsupp scan fragments (c472-c475) ran at 0.21 s/GB while the other (c464-c467) ran at 0.05 s/GB in the same run; that one fragment is 348 ms = 32% of the span and tracks the run-to-run spread (MFS-5, unverified, cause unknown).

**Proposed changes.** (1) Real FILES() cardinalities (C1) so nation/region are broadcast and never the shuffled side; note this does not by itself recreate the DELIM shape, which needs (2) remote runtime filters implemented in the translator/CN, mapping `THashJoinNode.build_runtime_filters` / `TPlanNode.probe_runtime_filters` onto the engine's dynamic-filter channel (`docs/super-sirius/dynamic-filters.md:58-94`); the FE already pushes them through aggregates (`AggregationNode.pushDownRuntimeFilters :448-464`). Confidence high on the diagnosis, low on the effort of (2). A CN->FE "re-plan" request does not exist and is not a feasible interim.

#### P3 (confirmed with a corrected mechanism). The FE's BROADCAST vs SHUFFLE choice is data-blind; on 4 CNs it shuffles the large table and keeps only narrow-key broadcasts

**Measured.** With 4 CNs alive, 16 of the 27 broadcast joins in the 15 passing queries flip to PARTITIONED (plan-summary.txt vs plan-summary-4cn.txt); q20 and q22 are unchanged. The big movers on 4 CNs (card-compare-cn4.txt, cn4-cnlog.json per-stream nixl bytes, cn4-transmits.txt):

| query | shuffled / broadcast stream | actual rows | nixl GB per run | what a size-aware plan would move (measured 1-CN parked size of the small side) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| q03 | exch 2 SHUFFLE lineitem | 3,234,397,656 | 58.2 of 60.34 | broadcast orders x customer, 2.33 GB parked (cn1-ops.txt) -> ~7 GB |
| q10 | exch 8 SHUFFLE lineitem; exch 5 SHUFFLE customer | 1,480,675,200; 150,000,000 | 26.65 + 19.15 of 48.04 | broadcast filtered orders 0.70 GB and lineitem x orders 2.29 GB -> ~9 GB |
| q12 | exch 1 SHUFFLE orders | 1,500,000,000 | 23.09 of 23.47 | broadcast filtered lineitem 0.51 GB -> ~1.5 GB |
| q07 | exch 8 SHUFFLE lineitem (build vs a 799,746-row probe); exch 13 SHUFFLE orders; exch 17 BROADCAST customer | 1,822,871,264; 1,500,000,000; 600,000,000 (150M x 4) | 43.75 + 13.50 + 3.71 of 69.01 | broadcast supplier x nation (~800K rows) and nation |
| q22 | exch 10 BROADCAST orders `o_custkey` | 6,000,000,000 (1.5B x 4) | 18.56 | build on the ~6M filtered customers (RIGHT ANTI), see P5 |
| q04 | exch 5 SHUFFLE lineitem (LEFT SEMI build) | 3,793,363,900 | 22.76 of 23.64 | RIGHT SEMI with the 57M filtered orders as build |
| q19 | exch 4 SHUFFLE lineitem | 128,557,109 | 2.70 | broadcast filtered part 0.02 GB; no measurable cost today |

Drain time on the critical path at 4 CNs (finding B5): q03 0.28 s of a 1.42 s span (20%), q10 0.26-0.29 s of 1.48 (17-19%), q12 0.12 of 1.08 (11%), q19 and q14 4-6%.

**The shuffle keys are stats-blind too (measured, low cost today).** When the FE flips a join to PARTITIONED it hashes on the join key regardless of its domain. q11 at 4 CNs shuffles 10,000,000 supplier rows on `s_nationkey` (exch 4) to meet the single GERMANY row of nation (exch 2 declared 0/0/1/0 rows per CN), instead of broadcasting that one row; per-CN supplier shares are 3,199,441 / 1,200,355 / 3,201,347 / 2,398,857 (cn4-cnlog.json q11.r1 `declared_cardinalities`), and the same shape repeats for the HAVING subquery (exch 15/17). q07's exch 20 shuffles 145.7M rows on `c_nationkey` (25 values) and lands 46.6M / 35.0M / 46.6M / 17.5M per CN (2.7x skew; cn4-cnlog.json q07.r1 stream 20); q02's exch 31 on `n_regionkey` (5 values) lands 480.0M / 160.0M / 160.0M / 0 (P2). Bytes moved are small for q11 (0.40 GB per run) and q07's stream 20 (3.77 GB), so no wall-clock loss was measured from the skew itself; it is listed because a `hash(key) mod N` shuffle on a key with fewer distinct values than a few times N cannot balance, and real cardinalities (C1) plus NDV would let the FE prefer broadcasting the tiny side.

**Mechanism, corrected by the source skeptic.** The cited term `CostModel.visitPhysicalDistribution` BROADCAST = `outputSize * aliveBackendNumber` (`CostModel.java:419-424`) is inert in this deployment: the Sirius CNs register as COMPUTE NODEs (`experimental/starrocks/src/lib.rs:210-212` `ALTER SYSTEM ADD COMPUTE NODE`; cn4/cluster.log:201 `run_mode is shared_data`), and `ctx.getAliveBackendNumber()` counts only BACKENDs (`system/SystemInfoService.java:1047`), so it is 0. The node count enters through `HashJoinCostModel.getMemCost` (`sql/optimizer/cost/HashJoinCostModel.java:115-127`: `beNum = max(1, aliveBackendNumber + aliveComputeNodeNumber)` in shared-data mode, `memCost = rightOutput * beNum` for BROADCAST, weight 2 in `CostModel.getRealCost`). With every child at 1 row, `Statistics.getOutputSize` is the sum of projected type widths, and the rule reduces to: broadcast the right side iff its row width is below roughly the left width at 1 CN, and below roughly a quarter of it at 4 CNs. This reproduces every observed decision (q03: build 16 B vs probe 24 B -> BROADCAST at 1 CN, PARTITIONED at 4; customer 4 B vs orders 20 B -> BROADCAST at both; the survivors q22 `o_custkey` 4 B, q07 `c_custkey+c_nationkey`, q02 `ps_partkey+min` are the narrow ones). `checkBroadcastRowCountLimit` (`task/EnforceAndCostTask.java:281-325`) never fires because it needs `rightChildStats.getOutputRowCount() > 15,000,000` (`SessionVariable.java:1833`).

**What a row-count-only fix would and would not do (inference, hand computation of the FE cost code, medium confidence).** Giving FILES() scans a row count but leaving column stats UNKNOWN makes the FE estimate a join output as `max(L, R)` and range predicates at 0.5, so orders x customer in q03 is estimated at 375M-750M rows. That *arms* `checkBroadcastRowCountLimit` against the broadcast the finding wants: broadcast is rejected when the right side is > 15M rows and the left is less than 10x its bytes (`EnforceAndCostTask.java:324-325`). Result: q12 and q19 flip to BROADCAST (saving ~26 GB), q03 and q10's customer join stay PARTITIONED, q14 stays a wash. Getting the q03/q10 plans additionally requires raising `broadcast_row_limit` / `broadcast_right_table_scale_factor` (`SessionVariable.java:1833-1836`), or column statistics (NDV) for FILES(), or neutralising the probe-cache penalty in `HashJoinCostModel` (`BROADCAST_MAT_RATIO` 12 vs `SHUFFLE_MAX_RATIO` 3).

**Existing levers.** SQL join hints `JOIN [BROADCAST|SHUFFLE]` are honoured (`sql/parser/AstBuilder.java:6567-6575`, `JoinHelper.java:344-349`), but the grammar accepts them only in explicit `JOIN ... ON` syntax, not the kit's comma joins, and a hint disables reorder/commutativity for that join. `broadcast_row_limit = 0` forces shuffle everywhere (`EnforceAndCostTask.java:312-314`), which would help q22/q07/q02 and hurt q03/q12/q19. `cbo_debug_alive_backend_number` (`SessionVariable.java:1823`) changes only the BE count and cannot reproduce the 1-CN plan at 4 CNs.

Confidence: high on the flip and the byte inflation; medium on the corrected cost arithmetic (not executed in the FE).

#### P4 (confirmed, impact narrowed). Every CN statement pays a fixed ~120-270 ms before the first fragment runs

**Measured** (first `fragment run started` minus `runs.csv start_utc`, agent-notes/mfs3_decomp.py, warm runs): cn1 q02 195/189 ms, q11 233/227, q15 193/190, q22 199/136; cn4 q02 175/200, q11 262/257, q15 206/211, q22 118/155. All 15 passing queries pay it: 127-239 ms (cn1), 118-270 ms (cn4). The tail after the last fragment is 2-8 ms. Standalone pays 9-22 ms, measured in-process.

Decomposition of cn1 q02.r1 (client start 13:03:24.267; cn1/cluster.log RPC spans):

| phase | window | ms |
|---|---|---:|
| mysql process + handshake (`select @@version_comment limit 1`, planned as UNION_NODE and refused by the CN) | +0 .. +13 | 13 (18-57 across runs) |
| 8 `get_file_schema` RPCs, one per FILES() CTE in the WITH clause (5 of them for tables q02 never reads); lineitem call busy 28.3 ms + idle | +20 .. +93 | 73 (median across runs 104 cn1 / 114 cn4) |
| FE planning, no CN activity | +93 .. +147 | 54 |
| deploy: 13 `exec_plan_fragment` RPCs in 6 topological levels, ~40 ms dead time after every multi-reply level | +150 .. +329 | first fragment runs at +194.6 |

Sources: `TableFunctionTable.java:264 -> getFileSchema():688-712` (one RPC per FILES() reference, no cache); `experimental/starrocks/src/file_schema.rs:62-70` reads every footer serially (60 for lineitem) and deliberately ignores the FE's `schema_sample_file_count` = 2 (`file_schema.rs:52-58`, `TableFunctionTable.java:114`). Deploy waves are the per-level loop in `AllAtOnceExecutionSchedule.schedule` over `ExecutionDAG.getFragmentsInTopologicalOrderFromRoot()` (`qe/scheduler/dag/ExecutionDAG.java:195`), root first, so the leaf scans arrive in the last levels and the whole deploy sits on the critical path.

**Corrections.** The head does not "cap the 4-CN speed-up": with it removed, engine-only speed-ups are q02 1.10x, q22 1.12x, q11 1.83x, q15 2.46x, so only q11 is materially affected. It is 28%/36%/9%/37% (q02/q11/q15/q22) of the gap to standalone, not the dominant reason. FE-side cost is ~215 ms (cn1) vs ~205 ms (cn4) for q11.r1 from the AuditLog, so it does not grow with CN count. The ~40 ms inter-level gaps appear only after levels with two or more replies on one connection and are most likely Nagle + delayed ACK on the CN's accepted sockets (no `set_nodelay` in `experimental/starrocks/src/brpc.rs`; only outgoing `prpc_client.rs:170`): inference, medium confidence, testable with `stream.set_nodelay(true)` at brpc.rs:114.

**Proposed changes.** (1) `file_schema.rs`: honour `schema_sample_file_count` or read footers concurrently and memoize by (path, len, mtime): saves 60-110 ms per query, high confidence. (2) Set TCP_NODELAY on accepted CN sockets (brpc.rs): saves ~40 ms per multi-reply level if the inference holds. (3) For 1 CN, test `SET enable_single_node_schedule = true` (`SessionVariable.java:3337`; `Deployer.deployFragmentsForSingleNode` issues one `exec_batch_plan_fragments` RPC, which the CN implements at `compute_node_service.rs:424-450`); FILES() qualifies (`FileScanNode` is not in `ScanNode.isConnectorScanNode`). Collapsing levels FE-side for 4 CNs is unsafe as written because stage-2 fragments carry an `is_cached` descriptor table (`Deployer.java:247-251`) that the CN resolves from a per-query cache (`compute_node_service.rs:954-988`). (4) Bench-kit hygiene: emit only the CTEs a query uses (saves 3-6 of the 8 RPCs; does not fix real users). Confidence: (1) high, measured share; (2) medium, inference; (3) medium, code reading only, not exercised (section 5, item 11); (4) high, bench-only.

#### P5 (not adversarially verified). Semi/anti join sides, CTE inlining, lost operator fusion, dropped dynamic filters

These were analysed by one agent each and not refuted or confirmed by skeptics. Evidence is measured unless marked.

- **Semi/anti build side (PC-4, SAJ-2, SAJ-3).** q04: `5:LEFT SEMI JOIN (BROADCAST) build=4:EXCHANGE<-lineitem` with 3,793,363,900 rows (card-compare-cn1.txt line 20); 30.82 GB of `l_orderkey` parked (cn1-quent.txt q04 `STREAMING_SINK in=30.82GB`) and 22.76 GB shuffled on 4 CNs. The engine flips it internally: cn1/engine-cn0.log q04 F00 `HASH_JOIN (id=6) type: RIGHT_SEMI`, build = orders scan, probe = lineitem stream, so 1-CN time is at parity (1850 vs 1896 ms); the cost is memory and exchange volume, not time. q22: `11:LEFT ANTI JOIN (BROADCAST) build=10:EXCHANGE<-orders` 1.5B rows to every CN; per-CN `HASH_JOIN(15)` 0.516 s on 4 CNs vs 0.588 s on 1 CN (cn4-quent.txt q22.r1, cn1 q22.r0), which is why q22 scales 1.13x. Standalone uses `RIGHT_DELIM_JOIN RIGHT_ANTI` with the customer keys as build (standalone/runs/q22.explain.txt). The FE has the commutation rule (`rule/transformation/JoinCommutativityRule.java:34-44` LEFT_SEMI<->RIGHT_SEMI, LEFT_ANTI<->RIGHT_ANTI) but at cardinality 1 it never pays. The translator refuses `RIGHT_SEMI_JOIN` (`node_translator.rs:1743-1762`: the match has no RIGHT_SEMI arm, `_ => UnsupportedPlanNode "hash join type is unsupported"`) although the Substrait consumer (`substrait/src/from_substrait.cpp:558-560`) and the engine (`src/planner/sirius_plan_comparison_join.cpp:245,273`) support it. Proposed: add `TJoinOp::RIGHT_SEMI_JOIN => (JoinType::RightSemi, JoinOutput::Right)` plus a `JoinOutput::Right` arm; small, high confidence on feasibility.
- **Anti join emulation (SAJ-5).** `LEFT_ANTI_JOIN => (JoinType::Left, JoinOutput::LeftAnti)` at node_translator.rs:1749 is an outer join plus `IS NULL` filter because `from_substrait.cpp:540-570` lacks LEFT_ANTI/RIGHT_ANTI. Measured cost in q22: `HASH_JOIN(15) in=6.59GB` -> `FILTER(16) in=6.93GB` -> `PROJECTION(17) in=0.22GB` (cn1-ops.txt fragment 832d7f224fc8), i.e. ~97% of the join output is produced and discarded. Proposed: add the two cases to `SubstraitToDuckDB::TransformJoinOp` and map them natively (engine has `JoinType::ANTI`/`RIGHT_ANTI`, `sirius_plan_comparison_join.cpp:242-246`). Medium confidence.
- **CTE inlining (PC-5, MFS-1).** q15 scans lineitem twice in two fragments (cn1-quent.txt:990-1000: `GPU_SCAN n=56 in=122.25GB` in fragments 567 and 566, run times 2253 + 2163 ms strictly serial per cn1/cluster.log `fragment run started/finished`, agent-notes/multi-fragment-small.md section 3 (the Quent walls 4.434 / 2.149 s include the first fragment's parked wait); standalone one scan, 2627 vs 4685 ms); q11 runs the partsupp chain twice (16.4 GB + 13.1 GB). `CTEContext.needInline` (`sql/optimizer/CTEContext.java:157-190`) inlines unless cost*ratio says otherwise, and with 1-row stats inlining always wins (`cboCTERuseRatio = 1.15`, `SessionVariable.java:1511`). `SET cbo_cte_reuse_rate = 0` would force reuse (`isForceCTE`, CTEContext.java:206-217) but the CN refuses `MULTI_CAST_DATA_STREAM_SINK` by name (`compute_node_service.rs:1068`, `:1519`). This is also the plan-level cause of the q15 wrong answers (section 1).
- **q13 lost DENSE_COUNT_JOIN (SAJ-4).** FE plan: `5:HASH JOIN RIGHT OUTER -> 6:Project -> 7:AGGREGATE count(o_orderkey) group by c_custkey` (survey/explain/q13.costs.txt); the Substrait keeps the Project (cn1/dump/plan-0339.substrait: `aggregate -> project -> aggregate -> project -> join`); `detect_dense_count_join` (`src/planner/sirius_plan_aggregate.cpp`) requires the aggregate's direct child to be the join. Measured: CN `HASH_JOIN(6) 1.406 s + HASH_GROUP_BY(8) 0.261 s` in a 0.558 s fragment vs standalone `DENSE_COUNT_JOIN(4) 0.066 s` (cn1-ops.txt fragment 286810da3429; standalone-quent.txt); `grep -c "Fusing COUNT-join" cn1/engine-cn0.log` = 0. Proposed: look through a pure-column `LogicalProjection` in `detect_dense_count_join`, or elide the pure-subset PROJECT under an AGGREGATION_NODE in the translator. Medium confidence; it is ~0.4 s of q13's 0.38 s gap to standalone.
- **q20 cardinality-blind pre-aggregation and dropped runtime filters (SAJ-1).** The FE aggregates all of lineitem-1994 by `(l_partkey, l_suppkey)` before the join: exch 9 = 304,124,949 rows on 1 CN, 639,885,819 on 4 CNs (card-compare); the lineitem fragment is 3.303 s of the 3.800 s span with `MERGE_GROUP_BY(4) n=6 2.903 s` (cn1-quent.txt q20.r1); the runtime filters the FE attached to the lineitem scan (`filter_id 2/3, remote=true`, survey/explain/q20.costs.txt) are dropped. Standalone joins lineitem with the 8.69M delim keys below the aggregate (`DYNAMIC_FILTER(25)` on the scan) in 2.958 s. Proposed: implement remote runtime filters (as in P2) or, as an interim, honour the FE's STREAMING pre-aggregation mode as pass-through in `agg_phase.rs`. Medium confidence.
- **q07 dynamic filter no-op on the orders stream (FWJ-3).** cn1-ops.txt fragment 772c72f753ea: `DYNAMIC_FILTER(21)` on the 18.38 GB orders stream ran at +0.097 s, before its build published (Quent task timestamps), `PARTITION(22)` input 18.38 GB (no reduction), `HASH_JOIN(24) 0.753 s` vs standalone `HASH_JOIN(34) 0.072 s` with orders pre-filtered 18.37 -> 1.49 GB at the scan. On 4 CNs the planner logs `Not wiring dynamic filter(s): build side carries neither filter nor opaque-build evidence` (cn4/engine-.cn1.log 13:19:58.309). ~1.0 s of GPU operator time, ~0.25-0.3 s of wall in the join fragment. Proposed: treat a declared stream far below the base table as filter evidence (`src/planner/sirius_plan_comparison_join.cpp:646-664`) and add a dependency edge from the DF pipeline to the build's publish when the probe is a parked stream. Medium confidence.
- **The engine's in-fragment re-plan works, but only inside a fragment (PC-6).** Declared stream cardinalities equal actual parked rows for every stream (cn1-cnlog.txt `cards[]` vs card-compare), DuckDB reorders inner joins with them (q19: engine built on filtered part and probed the 128.6M-row lineitem stream, cn1-ops.txt 6493-6546; q07: build/probe of three joins flipped vs the FE), but `STATISTICS_PROPAGATION` is disabled (`src/sirius_ffi.cpp:233-240`), so a FILES() scan inside the same fragment keeps its raw estimate, and the fragment cut is fixed before any of this. Also see C2.
- **Two-phase aggregation is cheap (AGG-5).** q01/q06 merge and result fragments 3-24 ms, hops 1-7 ms, 20-40 ms total post-scan; parity 1.04/0.97. The translator's decimal lowering shifts ~0.5 s of summed GPU time into PROJECTION and is the 9.6e-4 deviation source. Low priority.

#### Disputed planning finding

**PC-3: "the 4-CN BROADCAST->PARTITIONED flip is the measured source of the 0.43-0.59 scaling efficiency": refuted on the causal claim, plan facts stand.** The data skeptic's objection: the efficiency band exists without any data movement. q01 moves 0.00 GB and reaches 0.59; q06 0.00 GB, 0.56; q15 1.27 GB, 0.58; q19 2.75 GB, 0.53; against q03 60.34 GB, 0.48 and q07 69.01 GB, 0.43 (results-ratios.md, cn4-transmits.txt). Movement therefore accounts for at most ~0.05-0.15 of efficiency on the heaviest queries and none of the ~0.4 baseline loss. The baseline loss is measured elsewhere: per-GB `GPU_SCAN` Computing rises 1.3-1.6x on 4 CNs for every query including the join-free ones (q01 0.047 -> 0.072 s/GB, q06 0.067 -> 0.096, q14 0.069 -> 0.112; cn1-quent.json vs cn4-quent.json top_ops), and ~0.2 s per query is outside the engine span on both arms (P4). Two attributions in PC-3 are also wrong: q07's dominant mover is the 1.82B-row lineitem shuffle (43.75 GB), not the 600M-row customer broadcast (3.71 GB); q02's are the four 800M-row partsupp shuffles (38.5 GB), not the 472M-row broadcast (4.25 GB). q12's orders shuffle is off the critical path (sender Computing 0.255 s overlapping the compute-bound lineitem scan). Keep the table in P3 as the plan-level fact; do not attribute the efficiency band to it.

### 3B. Cardinality

### 3C. Backpressure

#### B1 (confirmed). Receiver-first rendezvous plus one fragment at a time turn every exchange into a full GPU materialisation

**Source (verified).** `engine.rs:278-280`: `// One request at a time until the handle (and its sender) is dropped` `while let Ok(request) = requests.recv()`; `run_fragment_inner` (engine.rs:486-720) does declare -> `build()` -> `relay_from` each parked sender -> `run()` -> park (engine.rs:697-716). `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:739-745 relay_from` throws unless the source fragment has run. `local_exchange.rs:248-283 take_ready` returns a receiver only when every expected sender is complete. The remote path is also park-then-export (`EngineRequest::ExportNext`, engine.rs:91-95). Inside the engine, `Fragment::build()` opens a `StandaloneQueryScope` that takes the single-flight `query_lifecycle_mutex_` (`sirius_context.cpp:1555-1596`) until `run()` finishes, so two fragments cannot be in flight on one context even if the CN asked (source skeptic; this makes "run sender and receiver concurrently" engine work, not CN work).

**Measured, q05 timeline.** All 11 `exec_plan_fragment` RPCs arrived 13:03:43.358-43.462 (cn1/cluster.log 4142-4202). Fragments ran strictly sequentially: nation 6 ms, region 9 ms, then the lineitem sender 5774 started 13:03:43.434 with `allocated=2304 bytes` (engine-cn0.log:49203, an empty pool) and parked 39 batches x 2.668 GB = 104.06 GB by +1.315 s (Quent data_batch Stationary events: 26.7 GB at +0.32 s, 66.7 GB at +0.88 s); first OOM at +1.361 s (engine-cn0.log:49221 `requested 748875880 bytes ... global usage 107374182400 bytes (102400.00 MB), peak allocated 3376381184, reservation 3318948864`). The supplier/customer/orders fragments started only after the failure at 13:05:24.632+ (cluster.log 6072-6305); the receiver of streams 7 and 9 never started (Quent shows 7 of 11 fragments). Receiver 5775 later ran in 73 ms and its output sat parked for 184.5 s until q08's failure wipe (cn1-quent.txt wall=184.502 s, Comp=0.128 s).

**Measured, passing queries show the same shape under the cap.** cn1 q07.r0: all 7 senders finished before the join fragment started (cluster.log 6807-7005); 59.47 GB of lineitem plus 18.38 GB of orders were parked (79.1 GB, 74% of the pool) with dwell up to 2.76 s. cn4 q07.r1: every `fragment run finished` precedes its first `transmitted batches via nixl`. Per-fragment run sums vs span (MFS-4): cn1 q02.r1 13 fragments sum 977 ms, span 1067 ms, gaps 90 ms (8%); cn4 q02.r1 cn0 sum 748 ms, span 1081 ms, gaps 333 ms (31%), the largest before receivers waiting for the other CNs' senders. The 4-slot executor idles during the many 1-task fragments (cn1 q02.r1: 133 tasks, Comp 2.9 s in a 1.06 s span = 2.7 of 4 slots busy).

**Streaming works within a fragment.** q21 fragment 2acb (ran after the failure) streamed a 123 GB lineitem scan through FILTER -> HASH_JOIN in 3.15 s with only 46.47 GB partitioned out (cn1-quent.txt q21.r0). Only the exchange forces full materialisation.

**Proposed.** Two routes: (1) on 1 CN, fuse local-only fragments before translation (P1, item 2); every exchange is local, the fused plan is the standalone plan, no engine change. (2) Streaming receivers: build once build-side streams are complete, consume probe-side streams while the sender still runs, run sender and receiver concurrently. (2) requires per-fragment lifecycle/task creators in the engine (the single-flight `query_lifecycle_mutex_` and the shared `task_creator_` reset in `begin_execution_window`, `sirius_context.cpp:392-395`) and a build/probe decision before the streamed side's cardinality is known. Confidence high on the mechanism; medium (1) and low-medium (2) on design effort.

#### B2 (confirmed, mechanism sharpened). Parked batches are invisible to the downgrade sweep, so every OOM cycle frees 0 bytes although a 160 GiB HOST tier is configured

**Measured.** cn1/engine-cn0.log: 17,917 lines `[downgrade] [GPU:0] downgrade request not satisfied and disk memory space is not configured; data cannot be spilled to disk` and 17,917 `after downgrade (0 bytes freed), reservation still partial (...) -- proceeding with partial reservation`; per query 2503/3603/5603/2103/2302/1803. Zero lines with non-zero bytes freed. `[host_pool] HOST:0 ... allocated=72351744` is constant through the q05 storm (the host tier exists: `HOST_MEM=160GiB` -> `sirius.memory.host.capacity_bytes`, `engine_settings.rs:111-116`; `1 host memory space(s) created`). The bench kit already documents "host spill is NOT implemented" (`benchmarks/tpch/run-abc.sh:1038`).

**Source (verified).** `src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112`: `// Repositories escape data_repository_manager_ cleanup so sender output outlives this fragment.` `_output_repos[id] = std::make_shared<cucascade::shared_data_repository>()` (and `_input_repos` likewise). The only registration path into a per-query manager is `repository_wiring_materializer.cpp:68-71 add_new_repository` (inter-pipeline ports). `src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp:223-232` TIER 1 iterates `_data_repo_registry.get_all()` managers only; `:294-300` TIER 2 the pipeline task queue (queued GPU_SCAN tasks hold no input batches). The warning at `:357-363` fires whenever no DISK tier exists and the request is unsatisfied, regardless of whether any candidate existed. `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:1062-1066 output_row_count` throws on a non-GPU-resident parked batch (the CN swallows it with `.ok()` and plans blind, engine.rs:564, 582-585); `:822-825 export_packed` throws too, which would fail the 4-CN path on a spilled batch.

**Correction.** The original clause "the sender's engine query has already ended" is not the operative reason. In q05/q08/q09 the bytes that filled the pool (104.30/99.54/96.42 GB) are the *running* leaf fragment's own STREAMING_SINK output; its query and manager existed, but a `GPU_SCAN -> STREAMING_SINK` fragment registers no repository at all. Finished-sender outputs account for 0 / 4.7 / 8.8 GB in those three, 38.2 / 68.7 / 77.8 GB in q17/q18/q21. The escape from the manager is the whole mechanism, and the receiver's `_input_repos` are equally invisible.

**Impact arithmetic (inference).** Spilled data has to fit GPU + HOST = 107.4 + 171.8 = 279 GB. Totals a working spill would have to hold: q17 ~160 GB, q18 ~166, q05 ~171, q21 ~195, q08 ~200, q09 ~253. Five of six would plausibly pass slowly; q09 is marginal after the 16 GiB staging arena and the ~34 GB host-pool peak. The original "host spill rescues only q17/q18" compared against the host tier alone and should be dropped.

**Proposed.** Register the streaming sink's output repositories and the receiver's input repositories with a process-level registry the downgrade executor sweeps as a third tier, including the running fragment's own sink (otherwise q05/q08/q09 still die). Make `Fragment::output_row_count` read a row count from host metadata and `export_packed` accept HOST-tier batches (the local relay already upgrades HOST -> GPU in `lock_or_prepare_batch`). Correct the warning to distinguish "no convertible candidates" from "no disk tier". Note the newest-first fairness policy at `downgrade_executor.cpp:204-216`; the candidate that matters here is the newest fragment's own output. Confidence high on the mechanism, medium that spill is worth doing before P1/B1.

#### B3 (confirmed). The reschedule loop has no feasibility check: 179 stuck scan tasks x 100 retries x 50 ms, re-reading the split each time, while nothing can free memory

**Source (verified).** `src/pipeline/gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:348 static constexpr uint32_t MAX_RETRIES = 100;` (comment: bumped from 10 for cross-GPU batch-lock contention), `:409 sleep_for(50ms)`, termination only by count (`:349-364`) or `_completion_handler->has_error()` (`:314`); `:263` proceeds with a partial reservation after 0 bytes freed. Each retry resumes at operator index 0 and re-runs `materialize_table` for the same split (`sirius_gpu_scan_operator.cpp:530-533, 592-593`). No knob: `exec/config.hpp` has no retry field.

**Measured** (agent-notes/skeptic-oom4/retry_stats.py over cn1/engine-cn0.log):

| query | stuck tasks | reschedules | first OOM (from client start) | last reschedule | wall to die (s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| q05 | 25 | 2500 | +1.61 s | +101.33 s | 101.5 |
| q08 | 36 | 3600 | +1.73 | +168.15 | 168.3 |
| q09 | 56 | 5600 | +2.38 | +232.41 | 232.5 |
| q17 | 21 | 2100 | +1.20 | +103.74 | 103.9 |
| q18 | 23 | 2300 | +9.29 | +54.14 | 54.2 |
| q21 | 18 | 1800 | +2.68 | +114.23 | 114.5 |

Offsets are from the client start in `cn1/runs/runs.csv` (q05 13:03:43.185); B1's "+1.361 s" for q05 is the same first OOM (13:03:44.795) measured from the lineitem sender's start (13:03:43.434). Every original task reaches exactly retry 100; the retry chain of q05 task 2567 is byte-identical on all 101 attempts (requested 748,875,880 B, peak 3,376,381,184 B; the retry floor raised the request from 5.80 to 6.64 GB while the grant stayed at 3.08-3.32 GB = cap minus parked bytes). Quent q05 fragment 5774: `GPU_SCAN n=2543 Computing sum 229.5 s` (about half of it is the 50 ms sleep, which Quent counts inside Computing), `Queued 2228.6 s`, `Reserving 99.9 s`, for 40 useful batches that took 1.3 s. The storm is paced by the single manager thread blocking in `make_reservation` (Reserving sum equals the retry window: q05 99.9 s of 101.2), not by the sleeps. Exactly one successful task finalised after the first OOM in each of the six windows. The six failures consumed 774.9 s of the 910.3 s 1-CN sweep (85%). Log volume: 89,580 of 152,097 engine-log lines are the five per-retry lines. `SIRIUS_QUERY_WATCHDOG_SECS` cannot detect the storm because each reschedule creates and destroys a task, advancing the watchdog fingerprint (`sirius_engine.cpp:113-125`).

**Proposed.** At the reservation gate (`gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:263`) abort the query when `retry_count > 0 && freed == 0 && retry_reservation_floor > reservation->size()` (all three are local there), or in the reschedule path when downgrade freed 0 and `global usage == usage_limit` and no successful completion happened since this task's previous attempt (`_tasks_executed` at `:310` is success-only). Keep the 100-retry budget for the contention case, which arrives via `rmm::out_of_memory` from `lock_or_prepare_batch`, not via the reservation gate. Message the engine can emit: "104 GB parked by this fragment's sink, 3.1 GB grantable < 6.6 GB floor, downgrade freed 0 bytes". Effect: each failure dies in ~3 s (q18 ~10 s because its own senders run first). Confidence high; this is a robustness finding, no wrong result is produced.

#### B4 (disputed: mechanism confirmed, causal claim refuted). Fragments of a failed query keep running and park output nobody consumes; the leak is 0-38 GB per failure but decided no pass/fail here

**Source (verified).** `compute_node_service.rs:449-476 cancel_plan_fragment` only calls `results.cancel()`; its log line reads `acknowledging cancel_plan_fragment (best-effort: no engine-side abort yet)` (:468) and the docstring says teardown "is a separate work item". `engine.rs:291-316` drops parked outputs only when `run_fragment` returns `Err`, and then wipes every slot process-wide. `ResultStore.query_failures` (result_store.rs:98) is recorded but never consulted on the sender path. A translator failure before the run (q16) drops the `LocalParked` slots without `drop_parked`.

**Measured** (engine-cn0.log `[gpu_pool] allocated` at fragment boundaries, agent-notes/refute-oom5/headroom.txt `base@start`): after q05 4.69 GB carried through q06/q07; after q08 8.83 GB into q09; after q09 31.56 GB through q10..q16 (seven queries); +6.6 GB from q16's parked partsupp scan -> 38.16 GB at q17's start; after q17 4.0 GB into q18; after q18 0; after q21 36.64 GB into q22 (q22 cold 4110 ms vs 943 warm). cluster.log shows the dead query's queued senders starting after `fragment run failed` (q05: 5773, 5777, 5776, 5775 at 13:05:24.632+, the first 0.25 ms before the FE's first cancel ack). Engine-thread time stolen from the next query: q17 -> q18 6.42 s, q21 -> q22 ~3.35 s, q08 -> q09 1.04 s.

**Objection (both skeptics).** "Directly caused q17 to die with only 66 GB of its own data parked" is arithmetically false: q17's F00 lineitem projection is ~120-122 GB (46 tasks x 2.65 GB; standalone `GPU_SCAN(3) n=46 in=122.25 GB`), above the 107.37 GB cap, so it fails with zero leak; the leak only moved the death from ~40 to 25 parked batches. Every passing query that ran under a leak passed with `oom_resched=0` (q06/q07 under 4.69 GB, q10-q15 under 31.6-38.2 GB, q22 under 36.6 GB). No pass/fail in this campaign was decided by the leak. The order-dependence risk is real but inferred: q07's own parked footprint is 79.17 GB; under the 38.16 GB leak it would need ~117 GB and would have failed had it run between q09 and q17. The cn1 timings of q10-q16 and q22.r1/r2 were taken with 31.6 / 36.6 GB of the pool occupied (the reservation-gate blocks in C3 need that leak to occur).

**Proposed (small, high confidence as hygiene).** Store `query_id` with each `ParkedOutput`; on `Err` drop only that query's slots; keep a failed-query set on the engine thread and skip its pending `Run`s (Err-time bookkeeping, since cancel arrives after the next sender already started); make `cancel_plan_fragment` drop the cancelled query's parked outputs and dequeue its fragments (needs a `LocalExchange` removal by query; today removals happen only in `take_ready`, local_exchange.rs:284-308); in `run_ready_fragment`'s Err arm `drop_parked` the slots already in hand when translation fails.

#### B5 (confirmed, proposals corrected). Shuffle drains are serialised after the fragment finishes, and 84-88% of each drain is `export_packed` on the engine thread at ~63 GB/s

**Measured, cn4 q03.r1** (cn4/cluster.log): each lineitem sender finished at +0.610..0.684 s, then performed 3 sequential transmits of 4.82-4.89 GB, each `elapsed_ms=92-98 lease_ms=1-2 write_ms=6-8` (600-717 GB/s write), completing at +95/+190/+283 ms after finish; the next fragment on that CN (customer scan) started 0.1-0.3 ms after the last transmit on all 4 CNs. Same pattern in q03.r0/r2 and in q10.r1 (lineitem 0.145-0.159 s, customer 0.083-0.102 s), q12.r1 (0.115-0.125 s), q19.r1 (0.055-0.078 s). The Quent staging-lease probe times the pack directly: 48-52 sender-side leases per CN of ~311 MB, pack median 4.9 ms per lease = 63.5 GB/s, non-pack (lease RPC + write + transmit RPC) 0.7 ms, so pack = 84-88% of the drain for q03 (74-82% q10/q12, 18-32% q19 with 7 MB batches). Receiver-side unpack of the same frames: 0.14 ms per 303 MB (2.1 TB/s), ~30x faster than the pack.

**Source (verified).** `compute_node_service.rs:1207-1219` comment: "one FIFO request channel into ONE transport thread ... the drains still run one at a time, in the FE's destination order"; `:380-392 dispatch_worker` is one thread; `:864-872 run_ready_fragment ... .and_then(FragmentOutcome::join_into_ready)` joins the drains before yielding; `nixl_transport.rs:713-775` drain loop (`export_packed_next` per batch, lease RPC, `write_and_wait`, transmit RPC); `engine.rs:813 export_packed_next = engine_call` served by the single engine thread (engine.rs:321-324); `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:~800 kPackChunkBytes = 8 MiB` with `cudf::chunked_pack` on the default stream (~37 `next()` launches per 311 MB batch). The serialisation on the dispatch worker exists because `SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH=1` was set (capture-cn.sh:12; default off); with the default, the same drain holds the RPC open and delays the FE's next deploy stage instead (`Deployer.java:236-243, 318`). Either way it is on the critical path.

**Corrections to the proposals.** More transport threads (b) or a non-joining dispatch worker (c) cannot deliver the claimed saving on their own: packs and fragment `Run`s share the one engine thread, so packs still serialise, and a fragment started during a drain competes with `ExportNext` in the same FIFO; the upper bound of (b)+(c) alone is the ~16% non-pack part (~45 ms per CN on q03). Packing during execution into staging leases (a, first variant) would need ~30 GB of arena per CN for q03 (15.3 GB sender-side + 14.5 GB receiver-side held 0.44-0.68 s) against 17.18 GB configured, and exhaustion is a hard failure (B6). The impact sentence "small fragments could have overlapped the lineitem scan" is wrong for the current engine (one fragment at a time, B1); only the drain itself, ~0.25-0.28 s of q03's 1.42 s span, is recoverable.

**Proposed.** Move `export_packed` off the engine thread (needs `ParkedOutput`/`Fragment` reachable from another thread; the parked map lives on the engine thread's stack, engine.rs:262-272) and make it faster: try a larger `kPackChunkBytes` or a single `cudf::pack` for GPU-resident batches (the receiver-side copy of the same bytes is 30x faster, so the 8 MiB chunking is the suspect; inference, medium confidence). Then (b)/(c) add value. Expected gain 0.15-0.3 s per shuffle stage at 4 CNs for q03/q10/q12 (inference). Confidence high on the mechanism.

#### B6 (confirmed). The staging arena is 87-88% full for q03 and q07 at 4 CNs, and exhaustion fails the query instead of applying backpressure

**Measured.** cn4 q03.r1 receiver on 9102: stream 2 frames 4.8885 + 4.8423 + 4.8506 GB + 3 x 0.146 (stream 9) + 3 x 0.03 (stream 6) = 15.1 GB = 14.1 GiB of the 16 GiB arena (cn4/cluster.log `received remote batches`); Quent whole-query occupancy peak 14.95-15.10 GB of 17.18 GB per CN at +1.28 s. Frames land at +0.71..+1.01 s and are consumed at +1.30 s (dwell 0.4-0.6 s while the customer and orders x customer fragments run and the receiver waits for all four senders). q07.r1: lineitem 3 x 3.62-3.68 + orders 3 x 1.13 + customer 3 x 0.30 = ~15.2 GB per CN. q10 6.4-11.7 GiB, q12 5.4-6.0, q14 <= 3.3, q19 0.7. Lease waits are zero (cn4-transmits.txt `lease_ms` median 0, max 15 ms in q12.r1), which is consistent with a non-blocking arena, not with "no pressure". Peak lease concurrency per CN: q07.r1 63-64, q03.r1 55-56 (cn4-quent.txt per-fragment `maxconc`; session-wide max 94, WORKFLOW-PLAN fact 13) against no lease-count limit, so the arena is bounded by bytes only; per-query lease counts and GB in cn4-quent.txt are time-attributed and can bleed into the next run (tooling defect AGG-6 below), which is why per-stream bytes above come from cn4/cluster.log rather than from the lease digest.

**Source (verified).** `src/exec/exchange_staging_arena.cpp:248` throws `exchange staging arena exhausted: requested {} bytes ... (raise SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES)`; `nixl_transport.rs:720 rpc_request_lease(...)?` propagates the error out of the drain; `compute_node_service.rs:1302 handle_staging_lease` has no wait or retry. The arena's own destructor summary never printed because the CNs were force-exited.

**Impact (inference, medium).** With the current FE plan the arena requirement for q03 grows as lineitem/N: ~SF1150 with `STAGING=16GiB`, or SF1000 with a 12 GiB arena, fails q03 after all the scan work is done. Broadcasting the small side (P3) would need < 1 GB of arena per CN for this family.

**Proposed.** Short term: document `STAGING >= (N-1)/N x largest shuffled stream` in the cn-tuning guidance and fix P3. Engine: make `exchange_staging_arena::lease` block with a bounded wait on release instead of throwing, so a full arena throttles senders; or let the receiver push remote frames into pool memory on arrival (`push_packed` is already a deep copy) and release the lease immediately, keeping only the per-frame row count for `declare_input_cardinality`. Confidence high on the occupancy and the failure path.

#### B7 (medium confidence, not adversarially verified). Per-task GPU_SCAN time rises 1.3-1.6x when four CNs scan concurrently, and at 1 CN the 4 pipeline slots bound the scan

**Measured.** Per-task GPU_SCAN Computing (ms per ~2.2-2.3 GB task, `*-quent.json top_ops`): q03 lineitem 102 (1 CN) / 134-145 (4 CN) / 111 (standalone); q10 90 / 100-119 / 96; q12 orders 107 / 131-146 / 117; q14 151 / 240-249 / 176; q19 85 / 113-126 / 98; q07 130 / 179-186 / 142; q06 100 / 138-146. Per GB: q01 0.047 -> 0.072 s/GB, q06 0.067 -> 0.096, q13 0.322 -> 0.498. q01 additionally shows 0.5-0.87 s stalls on 10% of splits on 2-3 of the 4 CNs, varying per run, with balanced bytes per CN (agent-notes/agg-only.md section 4); the 4-CN scan fragment is 1.43x (q01) / 1.6x (q06) the ideal quarter of the 1-CN fragment, which is 26-31% of the 4-CN wall. Aggregate read rates: q01 8.2 GB/s (1 CN) vs 22.9 GB/s (4 CN); q06 20.5 vs 50.8 GB/s, so the storage has headroom over what 4 slots pull. At 1 CN all 107 (q01) / 65 (q06) scan tasks are created within 9-50 ms and the 4 slots are busy 98%+ of the fragment wall (Queued median = half the wall); the memory gate does not bind for these two.

**Cause not identified.** The `scan_split_read` probe recorded counts only in the digest because `quent_bp.py` reads the wrong attribute keys (`bytes`/`elapsed_ns` instead of `compressed_bytes`/`output_bytes`/`materialize_ns` emitted by `src/telemetry/scan_telemetry.cpp:52-56`), and even the raw probe covers read + decode together (`materialize_ns`). Candidates: GPFS client contention on concurrent O_DIRECT streams from 16 slots, host/GPU-side effects, NUMA placement. The CN launcher cannot raise `pipeline.num_threads` because `engine_settings.rs::derive_sirius_config_yaml` emits no pipeline block (and pairs with C3: 8 slots would request 156 GB in the cold-start wave).

**Proposed.** Split the probe into read and decode, fix the digest keys (AGG-6), then A/B `SIRIUS_CN_USE_SIRIUS_DATASOURCE=false` and buffered reads / prefetch cache with the page cache warm vs dropped; add `SIRIUS_CN_PIPELINE_THREADS` to the derived config and sweep 6 and 8 on 1 CN with Quent on.

#### Disputed backpressure finding

**BJ-6: "memory backpressure is absent for q03/q10/q12/q14/q19 at both 1 and 4 CN; the 6-15x over-reservation is harmless because concurrent reservations are far below the pool": refuted on the 1-CN half and on the mechanism; the conclusion (memory pressure is not this family's loss) stands.** Objection (data skeptic, agent-notes/refute-bj6): 4 concurrent tasks hold 58-80% of the 107.37 GB limit, not "far below"; the reservation gate blocked 47-178 ms per run in q10/q12/q14 at 1 CN in all three runs (see C3), 0 at 4 CNs and standalone; the engine pool's running peak reached 92-99% of the limit inside q03.r0 and q04.r0. "No arena exhaustion" is vacuous evidence because exhaustion is a hard failure, never backpressure (B6). The proposed regression guard is inverted: a tighter estimate reduces gating; guard instead that `num_threads x per-task cold-start request` stays well under the limit. Cost today is <= 0.18 s per query, so the impact ranking (planning, CN serialisation, scan contention dominate) survives.

#### Tooling defects found on the way (AGG-6, high confidence)

`scratchpad/perf/sf1000/quent_bp.py:98-104` attributes staging leases by a +-0.5 s time window, so the last run of each query inherits the next cold run's first leases (cn4 q06.r2 shows 55 leases / 25.6 GB although q06 moves 64 bytes per stream; cn4-quent.txt per-fragment lease counts are likewise attributed by time, e.g. q07.r1's 1-task nation fragment shows 184 leases). Use cn4-cnlog.json per-stream transmit bytes for volume. `quent_bp.py:60-70 scan_reads` uses the wrong keys (see B7). Fix both before the next capture.

[feature.cn.dependencies]
# Provides protoc for prost-build in the Substrait crates on fresh CN envs.
libprotobuf = ">=7.35,<8"
rust = "*"
thrift-compiler = "*"

[feature.cn.tasks]
# Build libsirius from source via the repo-root build (creates build/release, which
# sirius-sys links by default).
engine-build = {cmd = "pixi run --manifest-path pixi.toml make",cwd = "../..",description = "Build the Sirius engine (libsirius) from source for the CN to link"}

# Engine-linked CN (default `sirius-engine` + `nixl-transport` features); needs the engine
# artifact, the `engine` feature's toolchain/libs (in the default env), and the local libnixl
# install. Every machine-specific path — the nixl/UCX prefixes (TOOLS_DIR, default: a `tools/`
# sibling of the repo root), the bindgen libclang headers from the repo pixi env, the system
# toolchain overrides that keep conda's CXXFLAGS out of the nixl-sys build — is derived in
# scripts/cn-env.sh so the tasks work from any clone path. NIXL_NO_STUBS_FALLBACK=1 (also set
# there) is mandatory: without it a broken nixl link silently degrades to a dlopen stub.
cn-build = {cmd = """
bash -lc 'set -euo pipefail
source scripts/cn-env.sh
cargo build --release -p sirius-starrocks-cn'
""",depends-on = ["engine-build","apply-starrocks-patches"],description = "Build the engine-linked StarRocks CN release binary",env = {NIXL_NO_STUBS_FALLBACK = "1"}}
cn-test = {cmd = """
bash -lc 'set -euo pipefail
source scripts/cn-env.sh
cargo test -p sirius-starrocks-cn'
""",depends-on = ["engine-build","apply-starrocks-patches"],description = "Run engine-linked StarRocks CN tests",env = {NIXL_NO_STUBS_FALLBACK = "1"}}
cn-run = {cmd = """
bash -lc 'set -euo pipefail

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Translate-only survey of all 22 TPC-H queries on the SF1000 paths with ONE CN (SIRIUS_CN_TRANSLATE_ONLY=1): the CN accepts and
# translates every fragment without executing it, so each query only costs an FE plan + translation; the client times out.
# Also captures EXPLAIN COSTS and EXPLAIN VERBOSE per query (FE-side plans and cardinality estimates).
SP=/tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad
WT=/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf; OUT=$SP/perf/sf1000/survey; DATA=/scratch/sirius/datasets/tpch_sf1000
QD=$WT/experimental/starrocks/benchmarks/tpch/queries
mkdir -p $OUT/explain $OUT/dump; rm -f $OUT/dump/*
source $SP/cluster-env.sh $WT
export NUM_CNS=1 GPU_MEM=64GiB HOST_MEM=128GiB STAGING=8GiB SIRIUS_CN_TRANSLATE_ONLY=1 SIRIUS_CN_DUMP_FRAGMENTS=$OUT/dump
M="mysql --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9030 --user root --batch --connect-timeout=5"
echo "##### SURVEY start $(date -u +%T)"
bash $SP/start-cluster.sh $WT $OUT/cluster.log
for i in $(seq 1 60); do n=$($M -e "SHOW COMPUTE NODES;" 2>/dev/null | awk -F'\t' 'NR==1{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i=="Alive") c=i; next} $c=="true"{n++} END{print n+0}'); [ "$n" = "1" ] && break; sleep 3; done
echo "alive=$n after $((i*3))s"
for q in $(seq -f 'q%02g' 1 22); do
  sql=$(sed "s#__TPCH_DATA__#$DATA#g" $QD/$q.sql)
  $M -e "EXPLAIN COSTS $sql" > $OUT/explain/$q.costs.txt 2>&1
  $M -e "EXPLAIN VERBOSE $sql" > $OUT/explain/$q.verbose.txt 2>&1
  before=$(wc -l < $OUT/cluster.log)
  timeout 20 $M -e "/* survey $q */ $sql" > $OUT/$q.out 2> $OUT/$q.err; rc=$?
  sleep 1
  tail -n +$((before+1)) $OUT/cluster.log | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep -a -iE 'translate|unsupported|error|fragment' | grep -av 'AuditLog\|INFO (' > $OUT/$q.cnlog
  nt=$(grep -c 'accepting untranslatable' $OUT/$q.cnlog); ok=$(grep -c -iE 'translated fragment|translate_fragment_logged.*close' $OUT/$q.cnlog)
  fe_err=$(head -c 200 $OUT/$q.err | tr '\n' ' ')
  echo "$q rc=$rc untranslatable_fragments=$nt translate_events=$ok explain_costs_lines=$(wc -l < $OUT/explain/$q.costs.txt) fe_err=${fe_err:0:120}"
done
echo "##### stopping $(date -u +%T)"; bash $SP/stop-cluster.sh $WT
echo "##### SURVEY DONE $(date -u +%T)"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Summarize StarRocks EXPLAIN COSTS output: fragments, joins (op, distribution, conjunct, probe/build children),
aggregations, exchanges, cardinality estimates. usage: explain_summary.py <costs.txt> [...]"""
import re, sys, os, json
def parse(path):
    t = open(path).read(); lines = t.splitlines()
    frags = re.findall(r'^PLAN FRAGMENT (\d+)\(F(\d+)\)', t, re.M)
    cards = [int(x) for x in re.findall(r'cardinality:\s*(\d+)', t)]
    # node lines: indentation + "N:NAME"
    nodes = []
    for i, l in enumerate(lines):
        m = re.match(r'^(\s*)(\|----)?(\d+):([A-Z][A-Z \-]+?)(?:\s*\(.*\))?\s*$', l)
        if m: nodes.append((i, len(m.group(1)) + (5 if m.group(2) else 0), int(m.group(3)), m.group(4).strip(), bool(m.group(2))))
    # fragment -> output exchange id and scanned tables (by column prefix under FileScanNode)
    PFX = {'l_':'lineitem','o_':'orders','c_':'customer','p_':'part','ps_':'partsupp','s_':'supplier','n_':'nation','r_':'region'}
    frag_blocks = re.split(r'^PLAN FRAGMENT ', t, flags=re.M)[1:]
    exch_src = {}   # exchange id -> tables produced by the fragment that outputs it
    frag_tables = {}
    for fb in frag_blocks:
        fid = re.match(r'(\d+)', fb).group(1)
        m = re.search(r'OutPut Exchange Id: (\d+)', fb)
        tabs = set()
        for scan in re.finditer(r'\d+:FileScanNode\n((?:.*\n){1,40}?)(?=\n\s*\n|\d+:|PLAN FRAGMENT|\Z)', fb):
            for col in re.findall(r'\* (ps_|l_|o_|c_|p_|s_|n_|r_)', scan.group(1)): tabs.add(PFX[col])
        # exchanges consumed inside this fragment carry their sources too
        for eid in re.findall(r'(\d+):(?:MERGING-)?EXCHANGE', fb): tabs |= set(exch_src.get(eid, set()))
        frag_tables[fid] = tabs
        if m: exch_src[str(int(m.group(1)))] = tabs
    joins = []
    for idx, (i, ind, nid, name, right) in enumerate(nodes):
        if 'JOIN' not in name: continue
        body = '\n'.join(lines[i+1:i+40])
        op = re.search(r'join op: ([^\n]+)', body); conj = re.findall(r'equal join conjunct: ([^\n]+)', body)
        later = nodes[idx+1:]
        rk = next((n for n in later if n[4] and n[1] > ind), None)
        # probe child: first later node at the join's own indentation that is not a build child
        pk = next((n for n in later if not n[4] and n[1] == ind), None)
        def desc(n):
            if n is None: return '?'
            src = ''
            if 'EXCHANGE' in n[3]:
                src = '<-' + '+'.join(sorted(exch_src.get(str(n[2]), []))) if exch_src.get(str(n[2])) else ''
            return f"{n[2]}:{n[3]}{src}"
        joins.append({'node': nid, 'op': op.group(1).strip() if op else name, 'conjuncts': [c.strip() for c in conj],
                      'probe_child': desc(pk), 'build_child': desc(rk)})
    aggs = re.findall(r'(\d+):AGGREGATE \(([a-z ]+)\)', t)
    exch = re.findall(r'(\d+):(?:MERGING-)?EXCHANGE\n\s*distribution type: ([A-Z_]+)', t)
    scans = re.findall(r'(\d+):FileScanNode', t)
    tables = re.findall(r'file://[^/]*/[^/]*/[^/]*/[^/]*/([a-z]+)/\*', t)  # weak; FILES path may not appear in COSTS
    topn = re.findall(r'(\d+):TOP-N', t)
    return {'query': os.path.basename(path).split('.')[0], 'fragments': len(frags), 'nodes': len(nodes), 'scans': len(scans),
            'joins': joins, 'aggs': [f"{n}:{p}" for n, p in aggs], 'exchanges': [f"{n}:{d}" for n, d in exch], 'topn': topn,
            'cardinalities': {'n': len(cards), 'all_one': all(c == 1 for c in cards), 'max': max(cards) if cards else None}}
if __name__ == '__main__':
    out = [parse(p) for p in sys.argv[1:]]
    if len(out) == 1: print(json.dumps(out[0], indent=1)); sys.exit()
    for o in out:
        js = '; '.join(f"{j['node']}:{j['op']} build={j['build_child']} probe={j['probe_child']}" for j in o['joins'])
        print(f"{o['query']} frags={o['fragments']} scans={o['scans']} card_all_one={o['cardinalities']['all_one']} aggs={','.join(o['aggs'])} exch={','.join(o['exchanges'])}\n    joins: {js}")

# Design: real FILES() cardinalities in the StarRocks FE (issue 3), "what upstream would accept" angle

Written 2026-09-03 against worktree `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf` at `45dab3be`
(FE = `experimental/starrocks/starrocks/fe/fe-core/src/main/java/com/starrocks`, CN = `experimental/starrocks/src`,
proto = `experimental/starrocks/starrocks/gensrc/proto`). Evidence root = `scratchpad/perf/sf1000`.
Every number is **measured** (named evidence file or a command run for this design) or marked **inference**.

## 0. Decision in one paragraph

Give every FILES() scan the row count the system already knows, through the abstractions StarRocks already has for
stats-less tables, in two layers that share one FE code path:

1. **Exact:** the CN already opens every parquet footer for the `get_file_schema` RPC (`file_schema.rs:19-25`); it
   returns the summed `FileMetaData::num_rows` in a new optional field of `PGetFileSchemaResult`
   (`internal_service.proto:647-650`). The FE stores it on `TableFunctionTable`.
2. **Fallback, FE-only:** when the field is absent (upstream BE, `fake://` in unit tests, non-parquet), the FE uses
   `total file bytes / sum(getTypeSize)` from the `TBrokerFileStatus.size` it already collected
   (`TableFunctionTable.java:611`), which is byte-for-byte the rule `HiveStatisticsProvider.getEstimatedRowCount`
   uses for Hive tables without statistics (`connector/hive/HiveStatisticsProvider.java:138-163`).

`StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode` (`sql/optimizer/statistics/StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676`) replaces
`setOutputRowCount(1)` with that estimate for `TableFunctionTable` scans. Column statistics stay `UNKNOWN` (no
min/max/NDV yet; that is a later layer). One mutable FE `Config` boolean, mirroring the existing Sirius FE knob
`files_query_whole_file_ranges` (`patches/files-query-whole-file-ranges.patch`), lets a reviewer flip old/new plans
with `ADMIN SET FRONTEND CONFIG` and `EXPLAIN COSTS` in minutes instead of a 40-minute FE rebuild.

Delivered as two fork PRs on `experimental/starrocks` (the carve plan's layer for FE patches and CN code): PR-A = FE
patch + FE unit tests + doc rows + CI patch-apply generalisation; PR-B = proto field + CN + FE consumption + CN tests.
No engine (`src/`) change, no translator change.

What this fix does **not** do, shown with the FE's own cost arithmetic in section 4: it does not by itself make
q05/q08/q09/q17/q18/q21 pass on 1 CN. The FE's cost model prefers shuffling a 6e9-row probe against any build above
~5M rows at 1 CN regardless of cardinalities, so lineitem still crosses an exchange until fix 4 (fusion or spill)
lands. Its value is that every downstream decision (build side, semi/anti commutation, broadcast guard, CTE reuse,
`broadcast_row_limit`, `exec_mem_limit`) stops being arithmetic on column widths (P3) and becomes tunable and
testable.

## 1. The defect and its consequences (measured)

| fact | evidence |
|---|---|
| Every FE estimate is 1 row for all 22 plans; actuals reach 6.0e9 | `survey/plan-summary.txt` (`card_all_one=True` x22); `card-compare-cn1.txt` (126 exchanges, FE est 1 everywhere; e.g. `q04 4 BROADCAST 1 3,793,363,900`, `q22 10 BROADCAST 1 1,500,000,000`, `q21 6 BROADCAST 1 730,806,711`) |
| Source of the 1 | `StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676` (`// cause we don't know the real schema in file, just use the default Row Count now`, `builder.setOutputRowCount(1)`, every column `ColumnStatistic.unknown()`), reached from `visitLogicalTableFunctionTableScan` (:374-375) |
| With every side at 1 row, BROADCAST vs SHUFFLE reduces to a column-width rule | P3: `HashJoinCostModel.getMemCost` (:115-130) `memCost = rightOutput * beNum`, `Statistics.getOutputSize` (:88-107) uses `getTypeSize()` for UNKNOWN columns; reproduces all 27 observed decisions |
| The six 1-CN failures are one plan shape: unfiltered lineitem leaf under a HASH_PARTITIONED sink parked whole (104 GB pool at death, 17,917 OOM lines) | P1 table; `cn1/engine-cn0.log`; `cn1-quent.txt` |
| `checkBroadcastRowCountLimit`, `JoinCommutativityRule` (semi/anti), and CTE reuse never fire at cardinality 1 | `EnforceAndCostTask.java:281-325` needs `rightChildStats.getOutputRowCount() > 15,000,000`; `JoinCommutativityRule.java:34-44`; `CostModel.visitPhysicalCTEAnchor` :563-570 (measured effect: q15 scans lineitem twice, `cn1-quent.txt:990-1000`; q04 parks 30.82 GB of `l_orderkey`, q22 broadcasts 1.5e9 orders rows x 4 CNs = 18.56 GB nixl, `cn4-transmits.txt`) |
| Row counts already exist on both sides of the RPC | FE: `TableFunctionTable.java:587-623` collects `TBrokerFileStatus.size` (`:611 brokerFileStatus.setSize(fileStatus.getLen())`; thrift `FileBrokerService.thrift:48-58`); CN: `file_schema.rs:19-25` reads the footer (`ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder::new(file).await`, `builder.metadata().file_metadata()`), and `parquet::file::metadata::FileMetaData::num_rows()` is one accessor away (parquet-59.2.0 `src/file/metadata/mod.rs:548`) |
| The translator does not read the FE cardinality; the engine's own statistics propagation is off | `node_translator.rs:1922-1929` (comment only; `grep cardinality` finds no consumer in the translator or CN besides the receiver-side `declare_input_cardinality`, `engine.rs:577`); P5 PC-6 `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:233-240` |

Consequence for blast radius: this change alters FE plan shape only (fragment cut, join sides, exchange type). Scan
split assignment is bytes-based (`FileScanNode.java:545-549`) and unchanged; in-fragment engine plans are unchanged.

## 2. Mechanism

### 2.1 FE: `TableFunctionTable` owns the estimate

`TableFunctionTable` (`catalog/TableFunctionTable.java`) gains:

```java
// total rows over fileStatuses as reported by get_file_schema; -1 when the node did not report one
private long footerRowCount = -1;

public long getTotalFileBytes() {                     // TBrokerFileStatus.size, files only
    return fileStatuses.stream().filter(f -> !f.isDir).mapToLong(f -> f.size).sum();
}

/** Row-count estimate for the CBO: footer total, else bytes / row width (Hive's rule), else 1. */
public long estimateRowCount() {
    if (!Config.files_scan_estimate_row_count) { return 1; }
    if (footerRowCount >= 0) { return Math.max(1, footerRowCount); }
    long bytes = getTotalFileBytes();
    int width = getFileColumns().stream().mapToInt(c -> c.getType().getTypeSize()).sum(); // excludes columns_from_path
    return (bytes <= 0 || width <= 0) ? 1 : Math.max(1, bytes / width);
}
```

`getFileSchema()` (:688-728) reads the new field right after the status check (:721-723):

```java
if (result.numRows != null && result.numRows >= 0) { footerRowCount = result.numRows; }
```

(jprotobuf-starrocks generates public camelCase fields from the proto, cf. `result.status.statusCode`,
`result.schema` at :721/:726; `fe-core/pom.xml:1128-1150` runs it over `internal_service.proto` at
`generate-sources`, so no hand-written Java mirrors the message.)

`getFileColumns()` is the schema minus the trailing `columnsFromPath` entries that `setSchemaForLoadAndQuery` appends
(:255-275), because path columns occupy no file bytes. `list_files_only` tables never populate `fileStatuses`, so
they fall through to 1 as today.

### 2.2 FE: `StatisticsCalculator` uses it

`computeFileScanNode` keeps its shape and takes the table:

```java
@Override
public Void visitLogicalTableFunctionTableScan(LogicalTableFunctionTableScanOperator node, ExpressionContext context) {
    return computeFileScanNode(node, context, node.getTable(), node.getColRefToColumnMetaMap());
}

@Override   // new: mirrors the visitLogicalFileScan/visitPhysicalFileScan pair at :655-662
public Void visitPhysicalTableFunctionTableScan(PhysicalTableFunctionTableScanOperator node, ExpressionContext context) {
    return computeFileScanNode(node, context, node.getTable(), node.getColRefToColumnMetaMap());
}

private Void computeFileScanNode(Operator node, ExpressionContext context, Table table,
                                 Map<ColumnRefOperator, Column> columnRefOperatorColumnMap) {
    Statistics.Builder builder = Statistics.builder();
    for (ColumnRefOperator columnRefOperator : columnRefOperatorColumnMap.keySet()) {
        builder.addColumnStatistic(columnRefOperator, ColumnStatistic.unknown());
    }
    // Column statistics stay UNKNOWN (no footer min/max/NDV yet). The row count is the footer total the compute
    // node reported with the schema, else total file bytes / row width, else 1 (FileTable keeps the old default).
    double rows = table instanceof TableFunctionTable ? ((TableFunctionTable) table).estimateRowCount() : 1;
    builder.setOutputRowCount(rows);
    context.setStatistics(builder.build());
    return visitOperator(node, context);
}
```

`visitOperator` (StatisticsCalculator, the block starting `public Void visitOperator(Operator node, ...)`) then applies
the scan's predicates and limit exactly as for every other scan (`estimateStatistics(ImmutableList.of(predicate),
statistics)`), so `o_orderdate` ranges, `r_name = 'ASIA'` etc. are estimated with the UNKNOWN-column rules
(section 4.1). `PlanNode.computeStatistics` (`planner/PlanNode.java:577-583`) copies `getOutputRowCount()` into the
`cardinality:` line of `EXPLAIN COSTS` (:398/:445), which is the observable the tests assert on.

`FileTable` (external file table, `visitLogicalFileScan`/`visitPhysicalFileScan` :655-662) keeps 1: out of scope,
noted as a follow-up in the patch comment (it has its own `RemoteFileDesc` lengths).

### 2.3 FE: one mutable Config switch (documented)

```java
/**
 * When true, FILES() scans are planned with a real row-count estimate: the parquet footer total returned by the
 * compute node with the file schema, else total file bytes / row width (the Hive no-statistics rule). Column
 * statistics stay unknown. Upstream plans every FILES() scan at 1 row, which makes every join side, broadcast and
 * CTE decision data-blind. Mutable so EXPLAIN COSTS can compare both plans without a rebuild.
 */
@ConfField(mutable = true)
public static boolean files_scan_estimate_row_count = true;
```

Precedent: `Config.files_query_whole_file_ranges` in `patches/files-query-whole-file-ranges.patch` (same javadoc
style, same `@ConfField(mutable = true)`, toggled at runtime by `ADMIN SET FRONTEND CONFIG`,
`benchmarks/pinned/restart.sh:35`). Default on: the patch does what its name says; the switch exists for
measurement and for the 1-CN caveat in section 7, not as a permanent mode.

### 2.4 Wire and CN: the exact count rides on the RPC that already reads the footers

Proto (`internal_service.proto:647-650`, new patch file `patches/files-schema-row-count-proto.patch`):

```proto
message PGetFileSchemaResult {
    required StatusPB status = 1;
    repeated PSlotDescriptor schema = 2;
    // Sirius extension: exact row total over every range in the request, from the parquet footers the node
    // opened for the schema. Absent when the node cannot count (upstream BE samples files and does not set it).
    optional int64 num_rows = 3;
};
```

proto2 `optional` on an existing message is wire-compatible in both directions: a stock FE ignores the field, a
stock BE never sets it, the FE falls back (2.1).

CN (`file_schema.rs`): `parquet_file_schema` returns `(Vec<PSlotDescriptor>, i64)` with
`builder.metadata().file_metadata().num_rows()`; `parquet_files_schema` (:62-95) sums the per-file counts while it
runs its existing name/type agreement loop and returns a small struct:

```rust
pub(crate) struct FilesSchema { pub slots: Vec<PSlotDescriptor>, pub num_rows: i64 }
```

Handler (`compute_node_service.rs:681-699`): `PGetFileSchemaResult { status, schema: s.slots, num_rows: Some(s.num_rows) }`
on success, `num_rows: None` on error. `file_schema_from_attachment` (:1683-1707) is unchanged apart from the return
type.

Cost: zero extra I/O. The CN deliberately reads every footer already (`file_schema.rs:59-61`: whole-set agreement is
the contract; P4 measured the lineitem call at 28.3 ms busy for 60 footers). Interaction with P4's proposed fix
(section 4 item 7 of the report): that fix must stay "concurrent + memoised", not "sample N files", or the total
becomes partial; the design defines `num_rows` as exact-or-absent, so a sampling CN must send `None`.

`build.rs` guard (:72-108, `require_exchange_proto_patch`): add a second `(token, patch)` pair,
`("num_rows = 3", "patches/files-schema-row-count-proto.patch")`, so a checkout missing the patch fails with the
one-line fix instead of `no field num_rows on PGetFileSchemaResult` 200 lines later (the guard's stated purpose).

### 2.5 Delivery

| step | mechanism | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Patches | `experimental/starrocks/patches/files-scan-statistics.patch` (Java: `Config.java`, `TableFunctionTable.java`, `StatisticsCalculator.java`, two test files) and `files-schema-row-count-proto.patch` (proto). Separate hunks from `nixl-exchange-proto.patch` (:786+ vs :647-650), so `git apply` order is irrelevant | `scripts/apply-starrocks-patches.sh` loops over `patches/*.patch`, applies or reverse-checks, exits 1 on drift |
| Local build | `pixi run apply-starrocks-patches` (pixi.toml:94); `fe-check`, `cn-build`, `cn-test` already depend on it (:96-104, :135-145); FE: `pixi run -e fe fe-build` (Maven, ~40 min, copies `conf/fe.conf`, pixi.toml:197+) | `.claude/skills/build-sirius-starrocks/SKILL.md:23` |
| CI | `.github/workflows/experimental.yml:52-57` applies **only** `nixl-exchange-proto.patch` by name before `cargo` runs; PR-B must change that step to `bash experimental/starrocks/scripts/apply-starrocks-patches.sh` (idempotent by construction) or the CN build breaks on the new field. The carve plan already lists "the mandatory `.github/workflows/experimental.yml` patch-apply step" for proto patches (step 5, C3) | workflow file; carve plan |
| Submodule hygiene | `.gitmodules:29-31 ignore = dirty`; never `git add` the submodule after patching | tpch-bench skill note |
| FE unit tests | `starrocks/run-fe-ut.sh --test <class>` inside `pixi run -e fe` (no pixi task exists; document the invocation in the PR) | `run-fe-ut.sh` usage |

### 2.6 Docs (no knob without a doc row)

`experimental/starrocks/docs/TUNABLES.md` currently has no front-end section, and the existing FE knob
`files_query_whole_file_ranges` is documented only in `benchmarks/pinned/README.md:50-54`. Add:

```
## Front end (patched StarRocks)

FE `Config` values from `patches/*.patch`; set at runtime with `ADMIN SET FRONTEND CONFIG ("k" = "v")`.

| Knob | Role |
|---|---|
| `files_query_whole_file_ranges` | Whole-file scan assignment for FILES() queries so pinned tables can serve them (pinned README). |
| `files_scan_estimate_row_count` | Plan FILES() scans with the footer row total (or bytes / row width) instead of 1 row. On by default; off reproduces upstream's data-blind plans for A/B with `EXPLAIN COSTS`. |

Session variables that only start to matter once FILES() has cardinalities: `broadcast_row_limit` (15M rows; the
broadcast guard), `exec_mem_limit` (2 GiB; broadcast builds above it cost x1000), `cbo_cte_reuse` (keep `false`
until the CN implements MULTI_CAST_DATA_STREAM_SINK, see below).
```

## 3. Files to touch

FE (inside the submodule, shipped as `patches/files-scan-statistics.patch`):

## 7. Risks (ranked) and mitigations

1. **RIGHT SEMI plans hit a translator gap (high likelihood, high impact).** `JoinCommutativityRule` maps
   LEFT_SEMI <-> RIGHT_SEMI (:34-44); `node_translator.rs:1743-1762` has no `RIGHT_SEMI_JOIN` arm ("hash join type is
   unsupported"). q04, q18, q20, q21 carry LEFT SEMI joins whose other side is now estimated smaller. Mitigation:
   land plan item 5 (translator `RIGHT_SEMI_JOIN => (RightSemi, JoinOutput::Right)`; the Substrait consumer and
   engine already support it, P5) **before** enabling the Config by default in the bench; until then run with the
   Config off. RIGHT_ANTI is already translated (:1750), so q22's commutation is safe.
2. **CTE reuse turns on and the CN refuses `MULTI_CAST_DATA_STREAM_SINK` (high likelihood for q15/q11, high
   impact).** Cost arithmetic in 4.3. Mitigation: acceptance runs `SET GLOBAL cbo_cte_reuse = false` (existing
   session variable, `SessionVariable.java:499/1506`, wired at `OptimizerContext.java:98`), which reproduces today's
   inline plans exactly; documented in the TUNABLES row; lifted when plan item 9 lands. This is also the fix for the
   q15 double scan, so the two fixes are complementary, not competing.
3. **1-CN broadcast-to-shuffle flips park a large probe (medium likelihood, high impact).** With real counts the
   guard rejects q03's orders x customer broadcast (72 GB < 120 GB), so lineitem (78 GB measured on cn4, summed)
   would be parked at 1 CN in a 100 GiB pool with 58-80% cold-start reservations (C3): q03 goes from 3.1 s to
   marginal or OOM. Same mechanism, smaller volumes, for q12 (orders 36 GB) and q10. Mitigations, in order: (i)
   `EXPLAIN COSTS` at 1 CN before any sweep; (ii) GPU-sized `broadcast_row_limit` (session, no code) for the 1-CN
   arm and a documented row; (iii) fix 4a (fusion) removes the exchange at 1 CN entirely and makes this moot; (iv)
   fix 1 makes a bad case cost seconds.
4. **Fallback estimator error (0.2-6x) inverts partsupp/orders and part/customer** (measured table 4.1). Only in
   fallback mode (no CN `num_rows`); the exact path removes it. The FE UT covers the fallback with `fake://`.
5. **Patch drift on submodule bumps.** Three Java files plus the proto; `apply-starrocks-patches.sh` fails loudly
   (`exit 1`). The Java change is small and plausibly upstreamable to StarRocks (it is the Hive rule applied to
   FILES()), which would shrink the patch over time.
6. **Load path shares the operator.** `INSERT ... SELECT FROM FILES()` gets the same estimate; harmless for
   correctness, may change load plan text. Existing FE UTs that plan `fake://` FILES() (`PipeManagerTest`,
   `StatementPlannerTest`) assert structure, not `cardinality:` lines (checked by grep), so none should break.
7. **Determinism.** Statistics are a pure function of file sizes/footers; plans are stable across runs. The fallback
   depends on compression (a different copy of the same table gives different estimates); the exact path does not.
